#2012. It's Golden Bells! England star Jude Bellingham follows David Beckham into underwear modelling in steamy Calvin Klein photoshoot

Published: 11:57 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 11:58 EDT, 2 November 2026

First there was Golden Balls... now there's Golden Bells!

England midfielder Jude Bellingham is starring in an eye-catching underwear campaign for Calvin Klein - almost two decades after David Beckham signed a famous £20m deal to become the face of Emporio Armani.

Real Madrid star Bellingham, one of the stars of England's World Cup campaign, shot the campaign for the fashion giants in the Spanish capital.

The 23-year-old posed in a series of pictures wearing the Icon Cotton Stretch underwear - which retail at around £44 for a pack of three.

'I really enjoyed working on this campaign,' said Bellingham. 'I liked the idea of "the icon underneath" – that confidence starts with feeling comfortable in yourself.'

His underwear campaign follows on from that of fellow Real Madrid and England star Beckham - famously labelled Golden Balls by his wife Victoria.

Beckham signed a three-year deal with Emporio Armani in 2007, shortly after moving to LA Galaxy, with the company revealing sales went up 20 per cent once the news was announced.

Jude Bellingham models the Calvin Klein briefs in a series of images released today

'Calvin Klein is such an iconic brand, so it was great to bring that idea to life in my own way.'

David Beckham models Armani underwear in an advert seen at Macy's in San Francisco

Bellingham celebrated his 50th goal for Real Madrid with a strike against Racing Santander

Bellingham scored his 50th goal for Real on Sunday, in his fourth season at the club since joining from Borussia Dortmund.

The star, who began his career at Birmingham City, netted in a 3-0 win at Racing Santander.

Wearing the No5 shirt in which Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bellingham has now scored one more goal than the great Frenchman for Madrid — in 76 fewer matches.

It comes after he scored seven goals at the World Cup - setting a record for the number scored in one tournament by an England player. It included the final goal in the third-place playoff against France, which England won 6-4.

'Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special,' said Bellingham. 'Not only for me and my dreams but also for the team.'

'It’s very important for all players to score goals and make a difference in games.'

#2009. Kaka speaks for the first time since San Siro tears: “Milan is second home to me”

One of the most striking images from AC Milan’s derby win over Inter on Saturday was Ricardo Kaka’s tears as he was welcomed on the field.

Saturday night was the night of Milan’s resounding derby victory – their fourth in a row against Inter – but it was also the night of Kakà’s return to San Siro. He was presented with a trophy before kick-off to mark his induction into the Rossoneri Hall of Fame.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a moment filled with emotion for all the fans present who chanted his name, but above all it was a moving moment for Kakà himself, who couldn’t hold back the tears as a montage video played on the screen.

Now, the Brazilian has spoken for the first time since that memorable evening as the NSS Sports Instagram page published a short interview with him.

“Milan is a second home to me: that’s the word that comes to mind when I think of this city. I’ve been truly fortunate to have so many great champions at my side, at AC Milan, in the national team, in Madrid: I’ve played with some truly brilliant players.

“The most elegant? Zidane, even though I didn’t play with him, but against him. The best moments associated with San Siro are definitely the victories, the Champions League celebrations in 2007, so many matches like the one against Manchester United or the one against Roma when we won the Scudetto.

“But there were also many moments, every time I entered San Siro and heard the chant ‘Siam venuti fin qua, siam venuti fin qua…’, I got goosebumps.”

#2007. Austin FC vs Portland Timbers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 06 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 08:59

Austin FC host Portland Timbers in a Major League Soccer Decision Day fixture at Q2 Stadium on Saturday.

A win would clinch a playoff place for Portland, while Austin, already eliminated, play the last match of Davy Arnaud’s interim spell before Jim Curtin takes over.

Austin FC sit 14th in the Western Conference and were eliminated from playoff contention by consecutive defeats to Real Salt Lake on October 28 and LA Galaxy on October 31.

Arnaud has been in charge on an interim basis since Nico Estevez was dismissed on May 18, and Curtin, the former Philadelphia Union head coach, takes over on December 1 or at the end of the season, whichever is later.

The Galaxy defeat was settled early, with Joao Klauss scoring in the 10th minute, Hirving Lozano in the 38th and Robert Taylor in the 48th to leave Austin three goals down before the hour.

Ervin Torres pulled one back in the 54th minute with a long-range strike for his second career MLS goal, set up by Micah Burton - who was making his first MLS start - and Jorge Alastuey, before Sergi Roberto made it 4-1 in the 66th minute.

Damian Las made two saves in the 35th minute to keep the score at 2-0 at that stage, and Riley Thomas came off the bench to make his MLS debut.

On a brighter note, Austin have scored in each of their last seven matches, having last been held scoreless by FC Dallas on September 20.

Myrto Uzuni and Christian Ramirez both have nine goals and would reach double figures with a goal on Saturday.

Austin also won the last meeting 2-1 at Providence Park on August 29, with Facundo Torres scoring the opener and Oleksandr Svatok netting the winner in stoppage time.

Portland Timbers are eighth in the West on 43 points, with 12 wins, seven draws and 14 defeats from their 33 matches, and a run of three straight victories has lifted them into a wild-card position.

Marti Cifuentes’s side were in a seven-game winless run between early September and mid-October, so a third successive playoff appearance in his first season would mark a sharp turnaround.

The three wins came against Charlotte FC, St. Louis City and Houston Dynamo, all of whom are heading to the post-season, and the Timbers scored nine goals across those fixtures.

The 3-1 victory over Houston on November 1 featured a 18-8 shot advantage, with six efforts on target compared with one for the visitors.

Vincent Janssen, a mid-season signing, scored his fifth goal of the season against Houston and added two assists, the first of his MLS career.

Kristoffer Velde scored his 11th goal of the season in the same game, and American Soccer Analysis rated him the most valuable outfield player in MLS outside Lionel Messi since the World Cup break.

David Da Costa scored the opener and took his team-leading assist tally to 11 from the corner that Janssen headed in for the third.

The Timbers rank ninth in MLS for goals scored but 22nd for goals conceded, and they have kept only two clean sheets this season.

A win clinches a playoff place and keeps seventh spot and a round-one berth, within reach, while a draw only secures qualification with help from other results.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

Austin will do without Chris Applewhite (quad) and Jon Bell (lower abdomen) for Matchday 34, while Zan Kolmanic is suspended following his red card against LA Galaxy.

Uzuni and Ramirez are both available to chase double figures, and Facundo Torres, scorer of the August opener in Portland, is also available.

Portland have six players listed as out: Alex Bonetig (shoulder), Brandon Bye (knee), Jimer Fory (concussion), Zac McGraw (back), Juan Mosquera (foot/ankle) and goalkeeper Trey Muse (concussion).

Janssen, Velde, Da Costa and Ariel Lassiter are all available again.

Las; Desler, Sanchez, Biro; Burton, Sabovic, E. Torres, Alastuey; Placheta, Gallagher, Ramirez

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Izoita, Caicedo, Da Costa; Lassiter, Velde, Janssen

Portland arrive with the clearer motivation and the stronger recent evidence, as nine goals in three wins against playoff-bound opponents sit alongside a front line in which Janssen, Velde and Da Costa are all producing.

Austin conceded three goals inside 48 minutes at the Galaxy, are heading for a bottom-two finish in the West, and have nothing to play for beyond individual milestones and the chance to give their academy players further minutes.

The Timbers have not lost in Austin since 2021, and their need for a result should decide a game in which both sides score.

#2003. FC Cincinnati vs Nashville SC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 01:11, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:06

FC Cincinnati will look to secure a spot in the first round of the MLS playoffs when they take on Nashville SC at TQL Stadium on Saturday.

Nashville head into MLS Decision Day with their fate already sealed, having clinched their first-ever Supporters' Shield.

Cincinnati are sitting in seventh spot in the Eastern Conference after winning 12, losing 11 and drawing 10 of their 33 matches this season.

Pat Noonan's side have come into form at just the right time, having dropped just two points from their last four matches since suffering consecutive defeats against New England Revolution and Columbus Crew.

Cincinnati recorded home and away wins in back-to-back games against DC United, before they played out a thrilling 2-2 draw against Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Orange and Blue then returned to winning ways with a narrow 1-0 home victory against Philadelphia Union, which came courtesy of Ayoub Jabbari's third goal of the season.

Having already guaranteed some form of post-season action, Cincinnati will secure a spot in the first round with a win against Nashville, but a failure to claim all three points will leave them open to being overtaken by Columbus and Orlando City, who currently occupy the two wild-card round positions.

The hosts can take some confidence from the fact they have won two of their last three MLS home games against Nashville, including a 2-1 success in September 2025 at TQL Stadium.

Nashville will already have one eye on the first round of the playoffs after clinching their first MLS Supporters' Shield with a 2-0 win over Montreal last month.

BJ Callaghan's side went on to play out a goalless draw against Philadelphia Union before coming from two goals down to pull off a 3-2 victory over New York Red Bulls last time out.

Sam Surridge netted a stoppage-time winner in that comeback success, which extended the club's impressive 17-game unbeaten home run in the MLS.

In fact, they have gone nine matches without defeat at any venue since losing away to Toronto FC on September 27, so they will be desperate to carry that undefeated streak into the playoffs as they continue to work towards their ultimate goal of winning the MLS Cup for the first time in their history.

Having tied the MLS single-season points record, Nashville will take the outright record if they are able to add at least a point to their 74-point tally in their final outing of the regular season.

Nashville will certainly fancy their chances of claiming a positive result after running out 4-0 winners in their most recent meeting with Cincinnati at Geodis Park in August.

Cincinnati defender Tyrell Malacia is unlikely to prove his fitness in time, having been forced to sit out the last three matches with an ankle injury.

The hosts are also without the services of Julian Malatini and Miles Robinson, while Teenage Hadebe is hoping to prove his fitness after being withdrawn with an apparent injury issue in the win over Philadelphia.

Evander is in contention to start the final regular season game after featuring as a half-time substitute last weekend.

As for the visitors, they have reported no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday's away trip, which should give Callaghan a full squad to choose from.

The likes of Daniel Lovitz, Edvard Tagseth, Alex Muyl and Warren Madrigal could come into Callaghan's thinking if he wants to manage minutes ahead of the playoffs.

That said, Surridge will surely be keen to retain his place as he looks to add to the 19 goals he has scored in the regular season.

Celentano; Smith, Hagglund, Hadebe; Mboma, Bucha, Nwobodo, Evander, Ramirez; Barlow, Denkey

Schwake; Najar, Palacios, Woledzi, Lovitz; Espinoza, Yazbek, Tagseth, Muyl; Madrigal, Surridge

Nashville carry a nine-game unbeaten run into Saturday's fixture, and while there may be changes to their starting lineup, we think they will do enough to extend their undefeated streak with a draw.

#2001. Puzzling Liverpool are not ready for the title, why Cole Palmer may have to leave Chelsea and Lisandro Martinez should have lost his spot long ago: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

Published: 07:09 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:20 EDT, 2 November 2026

In terms of points gathered, the Premier League title winner this season will be either Arsenal or Manchester City.

It's a two-horse race in which one of the horses has a bullet with its name on it sitting somewhere in a locked cabinet at Premier League headquarters.

We can presume, then, that Arsenal will win the title for the second season running.

Some are entertaining the idea that Brighton can have a go on our behalf. They have beaten Arsenal already at the Amex Stadium and now, after another brilliantly brave display at the Etihad on Saturday, they have beaten City too.

Fabian Hurzeler's team will not win the Premier League, though. Injuries, fluctuations in form and the fact they are playing in Europe will see to that.

Brighton have just played back-to-back games at City – the first in the Carabao Cup last week – and are off to Getafe in the Conference League on Thursday before facing Brentford back in Sussex on Sunday.

Liverpool are not ready to challenge for the Premier League title - and that is OK

It's exciting and it's fun but it's also a schedule that will get them in the end.

As for Liverpool, they are simply not ready. Not yet.

That was apparent before yesterday's home defeat to Arsenal, in which they played well.

Andoni Iraola's team also played nicely at home to City last month but lost that one too.

In fact, Liverpool have lost at home to both their rivals without scoring a goal. They don't score many against anybody, as it happens. Just 11 in the league which is three fewer than Ipswich and only one more than Manchester United.

So, no, Liverpool will not challenge for the title and that should be viewed as perfectly OK on Merseyside.

Liverpool have spent a lot of money since lifting the trophy under Arne Slot in 2025 but some of it has not been spent awfully well and last season was so very bad that they are coming from a long way back under their new manager.

There has been progress. Liverpool have recruited two sound defenders in Jeremy Jacquet and Ronaldo Araujo and are starting to see a return on Alexander Isak and, to a lesser degree, on Florian Wirtz, who has been nowhere near as bad this season as some people seem so keen to claim.

But Liverpool remain a puzzle in the final third. They play with nowhere near the structure and balance of Arsenal or the imagination and pace of City. Yesterday at Anfield was rather typical of how they can be. Possession, promise and power but a lack of calm intelligence and threat just when it really matters.

It may yet come. It is possible to see Iraola's influence. They would appear to have hired the right man to succeed Slot and that is half the battle.

But a third-placed finish, a journey to the last eight of the Champions League and a tilt at a domestic cup would represent progress for Liverpool.

As such – unless City escape their Premier League charges via appeal – this is Arsenal's title already and if that feels rather ho-hum and disappointing, it's for the rest of the competition to ask themselves how it has come to be this way.

Liverpool deserved to get something from the game at Anfield but warrant little sympathy for the manner in which they fell behind.

The home team's problems began when Virgil van Dijk took a goal kick and passed the ball a yard to his right to his goalkeeper Alisson Becker, who proceeded to give it away.

This is a common modern trend but no less confusing for it.

How have we reached a point where so many Premier League clubs seem happier for a goalkeeper to have the ball at his feet than they do an outfield player?

Van Dijk can pass the ball perfectly well. Let him do it!

Brighton are the league's top scorers with 24 and have had 11 different players on target so far.

That's more scorers than half the 20 Premier League clubs have scored goals.

Brighton celebrate a brilliant victory away at Man City - but they won't win the league

Nottingham Forest have to break free from their boom and bust cycle if they are ever to make serious Premier League progress and it feels as though that time is now.

Forest and their owner Evangelos Marinakis are on their fifth manager in the last 14 months. If normal rules apply, Oliver Glasner is in serious trouble after starting the season with just one win in nine games.

But Glasner was the manager Marinakis had wanted for quite some time. He first asked him to join in early 2024 at a time when Nuno Espirito Santo was struggling for results.

So now is the time for the Forest owner to look back at the churn of managers, players and indeed recruitment executives that has characterised his time at the City Ground and realise that something must change.

Glasner was unsparing in his criticism of the Forest players after Saturday's defeat at Brentford. In the same breath, he almost invited Marinakis to sack him.

But Forest's players could be forgiven for being confused and a little demotivated after so much change. Every time they lose back-to-back games, they must expect the manager to be sacked.

So it's time to shift that culture of uncertainty at Forest. Time to behave like a grown-up football club.

Glasner is extremely well paid by Marinakis. His annual salary is north of £10million a season and puts him up near the top of the list.

If Marinakis believes he has a manager of that standing, he should take his hands off the wheel and let him get on with it.

Oliver Glasner invited the sack from Nottingham Forest - but they should stick with him

Michael Carrick will do well to get much more time at Manchester United and there was a certain irony in Lisandro Martinez being the latest player to let him down as his team lost 2-0 at Chelsea.

Martinez – sent off after conceding a ludicrous penalty at Stamford Bridged – moaned publicly last month that United's recruitment hasn't been good enough in recent times.

Had it been any better, a seriously limited and unreliable central defender would have lost his place in the United first team a long time ago.

Carrick knows how this ends but what changes?

United actually played very well in the first half on Saturday and could easily have been two or three goals up by half-time, none of which will be of any comfort to their manager.

We have seen this movie before at Old Trafford.

Carrick will go, United's bunch of semi-serious footballers will raise their levels for a new manager and the club will start telling everyone they have cracked the code – again.

All of which goes to prove what we have known for a long time. Until the quality and indeed the mentality of the players changes at United then nothing else does.

Lisandro Martinez was the latest player to let Michael Carrick down away at Chelsea

Jamie Carragher believes Unai Emery is ready for a step up from Aston Villa to manage a club like United but has upset the Midlands club by saying so.

A Villa statement threatening to sue Carragher for his comments was simply embarrassing.

Carragher's language on the Stick to Football podcast was coarse and he may regret that but it was hard to take issue with his view that Villa sit below United in terms of profile and status.

Villa have made fabulous progress under Emery but part of becoming a really big club is learning how to behave like one.

Cole Palmer now has 50 Premier League goals in 105 games for Chelsea. Only Diego Costa and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reached that milestone more quickly.

Time will tell, however, whether Chelsea really will provide him with the platform for success his elite level of talent really deserves.

For all that they seem to be moving in the right direction under Xabi Alonso, Saturday's performance against a team waiting to be beaten was still some way below the level a team needs if it is to launch a credible title challenge.

Can Chelsea provide the platform for Cole Palmer that his talent really deserves?

Palmer will be lucky to find his way into Thomas Tuchel's England squad that will be announced on Friday.

His form perhaps warrants it but Tuchel was unimpressed by his withdrawal from the last international gathering and is unlikely to have forgotten.

What, meanwhile, of Trent Alexander-Arnold?

With Reece James and Tino Livramento still injured, the return to fitness of Ben White and Djed Spence has nevertheless given Tuchel some options at right-back for big Nations League games at home to Croatia and away in Spain.

Jarell Quansah can expect to start in Madrid for the game that matters leaving Alexander-Arnold to yet again consider the wisdom of his switch from Liverpool to Real in the summer of 2025.

Alexander-Arnold actually started for Jose Mourinho as Real won 3-0 at Racing yesterday but it was only the fourth time he has done so this season.

At some stage, Alexander-Arnold is going to have to make a decision regarding his future.

Anyone who has seen Tottenham play this season could or should have told you that the improvement on last term was obvious, even when early results were poor.

The London club may well have paid top-heavy prices for new players such as Sandro Tonali and the Manchester City duo of Savio and Omar Marmoush and the value of those deals will become apparent over time.

But Roberto de Zerbi's squad has more depth and balance to it and is benefitting in particular from the improvement in players he inherited from Thomas Frank.

We all remember Antonin Kinsky's Champions League horror show as Spurs collapsed at Atletico Madrid last March but the 23-year-old goalkeeper has been excellent this term.

So, meanwhile, has former England international Conor Gallagher who looked like he had forgotten how to play on arrival last season but was impressive once again in Saturday's win over Crystal Palace, this time as a second-half substitute for Dominic Solanke.

The fuss made about some clubs failing to sell out every single home game is ridiculous given the financial strains currently being placed on families across the country.

Still, it's strange to note pockets of empty blue seats at Coventry matches given how long the club have waited for a top-flight return.

Home games are listed as sold out yet rarely seem to be. Fans say it's because it's too difficult to pass a season ticket on to a friend on days they can't make it.

It's not a good look for Coventry and feels like a problem that needs solving.

There have been regular pockets of empty blue seats at Coventry matches at home this season

Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka called on his players to show courage and play as they train after their defeat at Coventry pinned them to the foot of the table.

But the uncomfortable truth is that nobody in Regis le Bris's team has struggled for form more than the experienced midfielder in recent weeks.

Xhaka was a success story last season as Sunderland stunned the Premier League but needs to find some of that Player of the Year form quickly.

#2000. The Celtic 'rollercoaster' Mika Baur is getting used to & how he spends his days off

It is easy to forget that Mika Baur only turned 22 over the summer. The German midfielder displayed maturity beyond his years in Celtic's captivating Europa League victory over Besiktas on Thursday evening, chasing lost causes, contributing defensively, and progressing play forward when the opportunity arrived.

It was his finest performance since joining the club for an initial fee of £4.5 million from Paderborn in August.

Baur compared his first few months in Glasgow to riding a rollercoaster, with downtime away from the football pitch proving rare.

"There’s no time to think about it! We are playing every three days and I really try to fight and bring my heart on the field all the time," Baur said. "Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t, but I hope people understand as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

"But I really try my best. I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster.

"Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans, getting the call-up to the national team was a big honour. You feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost but I am getting used to it."

This is Baur's first time living away from home. He credits his partner for making the transition to Scotland smoother, even if chances to play some golf are limited.

"I’m grateful to my girlfriend as she does most things and makes it comfortable at home," Baur continued. "The club also have people who have helped us a lot to settle.

"But you don’t get much time – you get home and lie on the couch!

"It’s not all stressful though. It’s also nice to go somewhere new and learn the city, get to coffee shops and restaurants.

"We’ve been to the beach, we’ve been to Edinburgh, we try to see a lot on our day off.

"I also play golf – so I’ve come to the home of golf! I’ve only managed to get to the driving range though. When you are playing every three days it’s a bit much to play nine or 18 holes.

"My father and brother play so hopefully the weather will be okay around Christmas to maybe manage a few holes."

Thursday's win over Besiktas wasn't quite a hole-in-one, but it marked a pivotal forward step in Celtic's Europa League campaign.

Finally up and running after consecutive defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, Baur gave credit to a raucous home support.

"The fans helped a lot," he explained. "You could feel the energy. It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win – it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

"It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.

"There is always pressure to win here, to win every three days. That’s what we all want. In the last two games it wasn’t possible for us. We knew it wasn’t good enough but here we played well and deserved it."

"The win was important after some tough weeks," Baur continued. "But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good.

"There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves. We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift.

"It was important to get those three points and we deserved it. Hopefully we can go forward with confidence from this game."

Despite his stellar showing on Thursday, Baur missed out on Jurgen Klopp's latest Germany squad. He made his senior international debut against Serbia last month as the former Liverpool manager had named two separate squads for four fixtures.

Klopp's group was reduced this time around, though Baur will return to the under-21s.

"I can understand," Baur said of the snub. "There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

"We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

"I’m still with the under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good. European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see.

"I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time."

#1999. GdS: Necessities, dreams and surprises – the January mercato Milan have in mind

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is ready to do what is possible to strengthen the squad when the window reopens.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that the Milan owner is passionate, so while he got emotional after the derby win against Inter, he was also worried following the defeat to Bologna and the limitations it exposed. So, he is ready to give Ruben Amorim a helping hand, but where?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim said that, with the squad reduced by injuries, it’s difficult to press hard and play the football he prefers. We didn’t see that in the derby, but that’s another story.

Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic are the defenders who could use a union representative: they always play, never rest, and almost never come out early. Mario Gila is the other starter, but then Fikayo Tomori and Matteo Gabbia – the natural back-ups – are injured.

That leaves Filippo Terracciano and Sankhoun Diawara, who are more uncertainties than guarantees at present. A signing will arrive and Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio was the target in the summer. The asking price was €40m then, and the Rossoneri could offer it again.

The striker issue is a different story. Milan invested over €70m in Gonçalo Ramos this summer, a deal that is now viewed with some trepidation. It’s right to give Ramos time, but Cardinale has recently fallen head over heels for Nicolò Tresoldi, who scored a hat-trick against Inter in the Champions League.

Tresoldi has been a Milan fan since childhood and doesn’t hide it. Milan would gladly give him the satisfaction of playing for the Rossoneri, but Club Brugge wanted €50m in the summer and it could be more now. Moreover, the De Ketelaere and Jashari negotiations show how difficult they are to deal with.

Will there be any other surprises? A wing-back is possible if Amorim decides the left side needs more momentum, or Samuel Chukwueze finds some company  in the treatment room. A goalkeeper to give Lorenzo Torriani a loan chance is possible. With Cardinale, nothing can be ruled out.

#1995. Mansfield Town vs Macclesfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:46, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:16

Arriving at One Call Stadium as underdogs, famous giant killers Macclesfield will face League One's Mansfield Town in the FA Cup's first round proper.

The Stags have only been eliminated at this stage in one of the last seven seasons, though the Silkmen are in strong form, despite their lower-division status.

Nigel Clough's Mansfield enjoyed their run to the FA Cup's fifth round in 2025-26, and they will be confident of kicking off their campaign in strong fashion this weekend.

That being said, the Stags have endured a mixed season so far, and head into this clash having won two, drawn two and lost one of their last five games.

Most recently, Clough's side were held to a 0-0 draw by relegation-threatened Wigan Athletic on Tuesday, marking the second consecutive match in which they have failed to score, following a 2-0 defeat to Notts County.

Those blanks have left Mansfield sitting 11th in League One with 19 points from 13 games, though a push for promotion is far from impossible, considering they are just three points behind sixth-placed Reading.

A run in the FA Cup could serve as a morale boost for a playoff charge, and supporters will be expecting to see the Stags progress at One Call Stadium, where they have lost just one of their six league outings this term.

Meanwhile, John Rooney's Macclesfield are best known for knocking out then-holders Crystal Palace in the FA Cup's third round last term, but they will need to navigate a pair of tough tests to make it through to face another Premier League club this time around.

This may be the first round proper, but the National League North side have already beaten Redcar Athletic 2-1, Scarborough 2-1 and Anstey Nomads 3-0 to reach this stage.

Those hard-fought victories have only served to bolster the Silkmen's resolve to prove they are more than a mere novelty, and having downed Bedford 3-0 last weekend - their fourth win in six games - the club will be cautiously optimistic.

That latest success marked a second clean sheet in three matches for Rooney's men, who boast the joint-best defensive record in the sixth tier, having conceded just 11 goals in 13 fixtures.

Macclesfield are also pushing for promotion in the National League North, where they are third with 27 points, a tally that has them just two off top-of-the-table South Shields.

However, the visitors remain significant underdogs, even if they have only tasted defeat once on the road across all competitions this season, winning six times and drawing twice.

Mansfield will be without centre-back Baily Cargill once again due to a hamstring injury, while Kyle Knoyle was forced off against Wigan through injury.

In their absence, Luke Bolton could start alongside Adedeji Oshilaja and Ryan Sweeney in the Stags' defence, flanked by Nathan Moriah-Welsh and Jordan Bowery.

Further forward, Michael Smith and Rhys Oates could lead the attack, platformed by a midfield featuring Louis Reed, George Maris and Elliott Hewitt.

As for Macclesfield, they are missing left-back Brandon Lee as he recovers from a long-term leg injury that has kept him sidelined since last season's FA Cup second round win over Slough in December 2025.

On Saturday, Cameron Borthwick-Jackson could operate on the left of a four-man defence, next to Tom Wilson, Sam Heathcote and Ammar Dyer.

Roberts; Bolton, Oshilaka, Sweeney; Reed; Moriah-Welsh, Maris, Hewitt, Bowery; Smith, Oates

Macclesfield Town possible starting lineup:

Dibble; Dyer, T Wilson, Heathcote, Borthwick-Jackson; Ustabasi, Shrimpton, G Wilson, Kay; Duffy, Elliott

Mansfield may have blanked in their last two matches, but they should have enough to get over the line against a sixth-tier opponent.

Macclesfield are one of the strongest sides in the National League North and could put up a fight, yet it would still come as a surprise to see anything other than a home win on Saturday.

There’s a strong belief that the 18-year-old can become increasingly important to the club in the years to come, but the present reality is different and more complex. He needs to play more regularly, yet opportunities have been few and far between.

#1993. Jim Goodwin says Dundee Utd are eager to keep momentum going against Motherwell

Jim Goodwin insists Dundee United are raring to go against Motherwell following their unwanted free weekend.

After a morale-boosting 2-2 draw with Celtic at Parkhead which extended their unbeaten run to six games, the Tannadice side had to miss their next William Hill Premiership fixture against Hearts as the Jambos had a Premier Sports Cup semi-final match against Hibernian.

Ahead of the visit of the Steelmen to Tannadice on Saturday, Goodwin told DUTV: “We’ve had a really good week training, obviously with no football at the weekend. That can be a little bit frustrating because, especially off the back of such a good performance against Celtic, you’re desperate for the next game to come around quick.

“But we’ve had a solid week’s training. The boys have done seven or eight sessions over the four days that we’ve been in. We’re having to drag them off the training pitch at times because they’re so keen to stay out there.

“Hopefully, there should be a lot of fresh legs there and hopefully we can go and give a good account of ourselves and maintain this unbeaten run that we’re on.”

Celtic's 'Che Guevaras' should show their fellow fans some respect at this year's AGM Marink Reedijk lays down Aberdeen challenge to Hibs team after Hearts win

United’s last defeat, coincidentally, was a 3-0 loss to Motherwell at Fir Park in September where Goodwin’s side were reduced to 10 men in 14 minutes when Emmanuel Agyei was sent off for a foul on Alex Lowry.

Goodwin is reading little into that defeat. He said: “For the first 15 minutes I didn’t think there was a great deal between the two teams. But then we get the red card to Emmanuel Agyei and that changes the whole game.

“They’ve got good pace. With the man extra they can really find pockets of space all over the pitch and they punished us on the night. But it’s a very hard game for me to analyse because of the fact that we were down to 10 men for 75 minutes.

“So I think tomorrow, if we can keep 11 men on the pitch, that would certainly be a start. I think 11 v 11, it makes for a very entertaining game of football. Two really good teams, two technical teams.

“They’ve got that attacking threat and that bit of firepower at the top with the pace they have. But we also believe we’ve got real firepower ourselves and real quality in the middle of the pitch where hopefully we can get that bit of control that we want.”

#1992. Liverpool injury, suspension list and return dates for Crystal Palace: Ryan Gravenberch, Hugo Ekitike latest

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 03:58

Liverpool will look to respond to their latest defeat by beating Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds not only lost 1-0 against Arsenal in the Premier League last weekend, but they also lost 3-2 against Fenerbahce on Wednesday in the Champions League.

Andoni Iraola cannot afford to head into the next international break on the back of a third consecutive loss in all competitions.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their Premier League fixture against Crystal Palace.

Possible return date: November 8 (vs. Crystal Palace)

Ryan Gravenberch was left on the bench against Arsenal on November 1, and he was left out of the squad that faced Fenerbahce three days later.

Iraola confirmed that he was dealing with a fracture in his foot, and he has cast doubt on whether the Dutchman will be involved before the international break, though he has not ruled him out of featuring in some capacity against Palace.

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Speedster Jeremie Frimpong was brought on at half time against Brentford on October 17 but had to be replaced just seven minutes later with a hamstring injury.

The right-back is set to be sidelined until after the international break, and Iraola stated on October 19, "It’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it's going to be difficult to have him."

Possible return date: December 26 (vs. Hull City)

Striker Hugo Ekitike has been out of action since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April, and is going through rehabilitation following surgery on the tear.

The Frenchman is unlikely to take to the pitch for some time, but has been included in Liverpool's squad for the Champions League league-phase, and could return during the festive period.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Nineteen-year-old centre-back Giovanni Leoni is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his debut in September 2025.

Speaking on October 15, Iraola revealed that the defender has faced a setback, saying, "It’s taking more time than we wanted. The plan was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next [one]."

Possible return date: November 22 (vs. Manchester United)

Right-back Conor Bradley has been unavailable since picking up a major knee injury against Arsenal in January, though he is planning a return this autumn.

The academy graduate has yet to join team training, but is making progress in his rehabilitation and started doing ball work earlier this month.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

#1991. Aston Villa drop legal action threat against Jamie Carragher after Sky Sports pundit's apology for telling fans to 'shut the f*** up'

Published: 08:46 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:30 EDT, 2 November 2026

Aston Villa have dropped their threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher after the pundit apologised for telling the club's fans to 'shut the f*** up'.

The Premier League club hit out at the former Liverpool defender for making what they labelled as 'unacceptable insults' on the Overlap podcast last week.

The row had centred on comments made by Carragher in which he pushed the idea of Aston Villa boss Unai Emery becoming the next Manchester United manager.

It escalated further when Carragher doubled down, telling Villa fans to 'shut the f*** up' as he claimed that Emery would be interested in managing a 'giant' again and declared 'There is a chain in football.'

On Friday, Aston Villa shared a statement on club channels carrying the name of co-owner Nassef Sawiris, reading: 'Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

'Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.'

Aston Villa have dropped their threat of legal action against pundit Jamie Carragher

Carragher had been pushing Unai Emery towards the Manchester United job on The Overlap podcast and claimed that Villa 'will never be' United. (Source: TheOverlap/YouTube)

Aston Villa had threatened legal action on Friday, with Carragher apologising the following day

Carragher issued an apology on Saturday afternoon in an attempt to defuse the situation.

'I'd like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans,' Carragher wrote on social media.

'My language this week was clumsy & wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it's not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!'

Fans were left stunned at the response by Villa to Carragher's comments, seemingly innocuous linking Emery, who is admired at Old Trafford, to the Manchester United job, which may soon be available with immense pressure on Michael Carrick.

‘I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year,' Carragher had said.

'But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

#1990. Luton Town vs Forest Green Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 05:05, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:20

Meeting at Kenilworth Road in the FA Cup's first round proper for the second season in a row, Luton Town and Forest Green Rovers will lock horns in a cross-division clash on Saturday.

The Hatters have progressed beyond this stage every year since 2013-14, though the Green have only lost one of their last seven matches.

Jack Wilshere's Luton are in the hunt for promotion from League One, and a strong run in the FA Cup could inspire the team in their push.

The Hatters arrive for Saturday's cup clash unbeaten in five games, winning four on the bounce prior to a 1-1 draw with Huddersfield on Tuesday.

That stalemate has Wilshere's side fourth in the third tier with 24 points after 14 matchdays, just two points behind second-placed Stockport County.

Luton's commendable campaign so far has been built on their attacking prowess, and it is notable that top-of-the-table Huddersfield are the only club to have outscored their tally of 26 goals in League One.

Saturday's hosts will be expecting to progress against their lower-tier opponents, though Wilshere is hoping for a more straightforward victory than last season's 4-3 first-round triumph over Forest Green.

The Hatters raced into a three-goal lead through Lamine Fanne and a Nahki Wells brace that day in October 2025, only to require a 92nd-minute winner from substitute Gideon Kodua after Rovers fought back to 3-3 in the second half.

Forest Green are operating without a permanent manager after Robbie Savage left the club to join Peterborough United last month, though Jonathan Gould is in charge of the National League team on a caretaker basis.

Rovers' owner Dale Vince has said that there is "No vacancy," and the club have won twice, drawn twice and lost just once with the head coach role remaining unfilled.

Most recently, Gould's side followed up their 2-0 victory over Eastleigh with a 2-2 stalemate against Harrogate Town, a particularly frustrating result given the Green held a 2-0 lead at half time.

In the FA Cup's fourth qualifying round, Forest Green were held to a 0-0 draw by Chesham, before thrashing them 5-0 in the replay, courtesy of goals from five different scorers.

The nominal caretaker boss described that attacking performance as a "Tonic," considering the team had suffered from poor finishing across their six-game winless run prior.

Looking ahead to Saturday's first round proper, it remains to be seen whether the visitors can repeat that offensive showcase against higher-tier opposition, though fans will take heart from the fact Rovers have lost on just one of their six away days this term.

Forest Green Rovers form (all competitions):

Luton will be without versatile left-sided defender Kal Naismith, who was forced off after just 17 minutes against Huddersfield.

Filling the gap on Saturday, Wilshere could opt to start Harrison Ashby at right-back and shift Isiah Jones across to the left, with the duo flanking centre-backs George Johnston and Mads Andersen.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Nahki Wells may operate up top, while Kasey Palmer and Tudor Mendel-Idowu line up out wide.

As for Forest Green, they are missing striker Ricardo Rees as he recovers from the cruciate ligament injury he suffered in September.

In his absence, veteran Will Grigg could lead the line this weekend, supported by Kyle McAllister, Kyle Kelly and Bryan Ifeanyi.

Shea; Ashby, Andersen, Johnston, Jones; Walsh; Mendel-Idowu, Donley, Clark, Palmer; Wells

Forest Green Rovers possible starting lineup:

McNicholas; Abrefa, Mabete, McIntyre, Kuemo; Campbell, Clarke; McAllister, Kelly, Ifeanyi; Grigg

Luton are in strong form and have been impressive going forward this season, so expect to see them score more than once on Saturday.

However, Rovers could find the back of the net, too, considering the Hatters have been less than stellar in defence.

#1988. Ex-Rangers star signs for new club in second tier after weeks as free agent

Former Rangers midfielder Greg Docherty has signed for Preston North End as a free agent.

The 30-year-old has been without a club since leaving Charlton Athletic by mutual agreement near the end of the summer transfer window, despite having captained them to promotion from League One a year before.

With the Addicks continually strengthening for the Championship, he found himself out of favour and it was agreed he could move on in search of first team football.

Former Motherwell boss Graham Alexander recently took over at Preston and was tipped in recent weeks to make a move for Docherty, after admitting he was looking at free agents. That has now come to fruition.

Preston announced the signing today and Docherty told their website: “I’m really proud to be here, to have this badge on my chest and to be part of a club that’s steeped in history. When I told my family, they were all excited and willing me to get it done.

“I’m just thankful that we managed to do it. Coming down from Scotland and playing in England, Preston’s a very good team to get to for my family and I’ve always kept an eye on them.

Derek McInnes news, interviews and updates on the Rangers manager The quietly effective Rangers star McInnes says inspires dressing-room confidence

“I’ve always loved playing at Deepdale but haven’t won very often there, so hopefully that will change now. When I was an opposition player, I always found it really difficult. I’ve got family in the north of England and this move just really ticks all the boxes.

“To be a Preston player is something I’ve always wanted to do and I’m really proud to have finally done it.”

Docherty has been training with Alexander's side already and added: “From the moment I walked in here, I got a really good feeling from speaking to the manager and all the coaching staff.

“When I see how passionate the manager is about turning our current situation around, it excites me and I want to also help change things. I see real quality in the dressing room and I know we can improve if we keep working hard.

“The manager’s training demands are very high, and I’ve come in and really enjoyed it. I’ve enjoyed the soreness after it, I’ve enjoyed the tiredness after it, but I feel much better for it and all the lads do too.

“The boys are saying they’re getting fitter, which is massive in this league, and I just can’t wait to get going alongside them out on the pitch.”

Alexander said: “We’re really pleased to bring Greg in. He’s been a captain, won promotions and knows the game inside out.

“Greg’s vocal, fit and motivated, which are all the key things you look for in a professional footballer.

“He has settled into the group really quickly and has a real willingness to show what he can do.”

#1987. Paris Saint-Germain vs. Troyes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 06 Nov 2026 05:24, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 05:57

Paris Saint-Germain enter Saturday's gameweek 10 Ligue 1 encounter at Parc des Princes seeking a seventh consecutive league victory and an 11th straight win across all competitions.

The European champions have not dropped points in two months, and Luis Enrique's men are heavy favourites to extend their dominant run against Troyes, who have claimed just one victory in their last seven matches.

PSG enter every Ligue 1 season as overwhelming title favourites, but even many of their own supporters may be surprised by their current winning sequence.

Enrique's team have largely been unremarkable during the first half of recent campaigns before surging into top form after the new year; however, they appear to have found their rhythm considerably earlier this term.

There was a sense of business as usual when PSG suffered a 2-1 defeat at Parc des Princes at the start of September, leaving Les Parisiens with just two points from their opening three matches.

They have since turned the screw, beginning with mid-September's 1-0 success over Brest before victories against Marseille, Le Mans, Strasbourg, Lyon and Le Havre propelled them to the top of the Ligue 1 table.

The Red and Blues could yet be displaced by Lille, who trail by two points, or Lyon or Paris FC, who are both three adrift, but that outcome appears unlikely.

That assessment is reinforced by Troyes' position in the top flight, with 16th-placed ESTAC just one point clear of Le Mans in the automatic relegation places.

On a positive note, Stephane Dumont's team were in the bottom two before last weekend, when Mouhamed Diop and Ismael Boura scored to secure a much-needed victory after exactly two months without one.

However, facing PSG presents an entirely different challenge, and Troyes' return of four points from six alongside consecutive clean sheets could yet prove a false dawn.

A sixth league defeat for ESTAC on Saturday could send them back into the bottom two, although that outcome depends on Le Mans defeating Monaco.

#1986. Mikel Arteta convinced his Arsenal players he could read their minds before north London derby win - before revealing the truth behind bizarre stunt

Published: 12:31 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:35 EDT, 2 November 2026

Mikel Arteta convinced his Arsenal squad that he could read their minds in what proved to be a successful strategy ahead of the north London derby four years ago.

Revealed in Daily Telegraph reporter Sam Dean's book Arsenal: The Inside Story of Arsenal's Rebirth Under Mikel Arteta, the Spanish head coach played the trick on his players in the team hotel ahead of the 3-1 win at the Emirates on October 1, 2022.

Arteta, who is notorious for his use of offbeat coaching methods, reportedly asked the players to hide an object in one of their shoes and told them that he would be able to guess whose it was simply by looking into their eyes and reading their body language.

He promised the team that if he failed to guess the player he would take them and their families out for dinner, but if he managed to figure it out, they would be paying for him.

After he and his coaches left the room to let the players hide the object, he returned and studied each of the players, and 'even checked their pulses, supposedly to see which one of them was panicking the most', Dean writes.

When he guessed correctly that it was Brazilian defender Gabriel, the team reportedly 'went mental', a source in the book said.

Arteta convinced his players that he could read their minds ahead of their 3-1 win against Tottenham at the Emirates on October 1, 2022

Arteta is notorious for his use of offbeat coaching methods in order to gain an edge over rivals

Later that day, after goals from Thomas Partey, Gabriel Jesus and Granit Xhaka secured the three points against their north London rivals, Arteta and his staff revealed that they had seen them pick the player through CCTV cameras at the hotel.

This wasn't the first time that Arteta has deployed an unusual tactic with the hope of gaining an edge over his rivals.

Ahead of a game against Liverpool at Anfield during the 2021-22 season, Arteta blasted 'You'll Never Walk Alone' over speakers during training to prepare his players for the boisterous atmosphere.

In the summer of 2024, he hired a pickpocket to steal from the squad during an evening meal.

The pickpocket was disguised as a waiter during the meal and, after the dinner, Arteta held a pre-match team meeting where, at the end of it, he presented his players' stolen items at the front of the room.

That ploy was in preparation for a match against a team who tried every possible tactic to gain an edge, and Arteta wanted to adopt a 'pickpocket mentality', to always be aware of people trying to steal advantages from them.

For another game, Arteta did a pre-match team talk involving a lightbulb, as he wanted his players to shine and emit energy and light to one another.

As Arsenal pushed to end their long wait for a Premier League title, the club also installed the outline of the trophy in the entrance of their main building at the training ground. It was finally lit up in May, when the feat was achieved.

And during pre-season just past, Arteta revealed that he deliberately made his team late for matches by changing their route or meal times, as well as making the changing room hotter and reducing the number of massage beds in the hope of preparing the squad for difficulties on the road.

After signing new terms last month, Arteta revealed that his quirky practices began on his very first day on the job back in December 2019.

The then 37-year-old claimed he 'destroyed' an education centre at Arsenal's training centre, throwing 'the computers, the laptops, the cables' on the floor. He then requested his staff to reorganise the office in no time at all in order to prove their togetherness.

As Arsenal pushed to end their long wait for a Premier League title, the club also installed the outline of the trophy in the entrance of their main building at the training ground

In an interview with The Athletic, Arteta explained: 'I said, "Listen, this is what I heard. I don’t know if it’s true. But from a lot of different people, the sentiment is that this is how they feel about working in the organisation.

'I’m here to help you enjoy your profession and your life and the passion that we all share. If you want me to help you to do that, you have two minutes to put this in order and at least to be ready to work together’. And I left.

'That could have been my managerial career because if that would have stayed the same way, I had no job anymore!'

Arteta then outlined how he came back moments later and everything was 'immaculate'.

'Everyone was silent and had their eyes open and they were ready to listen. I said, "This is just the start. It’s something that we have to be in daily. Whatever we want to accomplish, we’re going to have to do it together. I cannot do it by myself. The issue that we have is much deeper than that, but the opportunity is infinite".'

Since taking charge in 2019, Arteta has overseen a notable improvement in Arsenal's fortunes, transforming them from a side floundering in mid-table to Premier League champions. He also took them to their first Champions League final in 20 years in May.

Seattle Sounders suffered a major blow in their push for playoff qualification last Sunday when they were dismantled 5-1 by Western Conference leaders Vancouver Whitecaps when the two sides squared off at BC Place.

#1981. On The Road: From Hagi and Popescu to Danny Armstrong... football in Bucharest has history and hope

Published: 16:31 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 12:42 EDT, 2 November 2026

The Starbucks at the entrance to the Old Town makes a familiar point by its very presence. The Half-Time Bar roars a modern truth incessantly.

Bucharest 2026, beneath the enduring glitz of imperial time and amid the clinging grip of post-communism, has become marked by globalism.

Starbucks serves its universal wares and the Half-Time Bar resounds to the English Premier League. Yet the fabulous gems of Romanian football are not far away.

The Muzeul Fotbalului sits on the edge of the Old Town. It is starkly modern. Its four floors offer strips to buy, interactive displays to goggle at and fiddle with, and shirts to admire or even covet. There are strips worn by Maradona, Pele, Cruyff and Ronaldo. But there is Romanian history too.

Gheorghe Hagi, Gheorghe Popescu and Cristian Chivu are rightly celebrated. The wonderful run by the national team to the quarter-finals of the World Cup is recalled in full, glorious colour.

There is a tribute to Helmuth Duckadam, who is the only goalkeeper to have saved four penalties in a Champions League final. When Steaua Bucharest defeated Barcelona in a penalty shoot-out in 1986, since you ask. Incidentally, Miodrag Belodedici is the only Romanian to win the Champions League twice, once with Steaua and then with Red Star in 1991.

Scottish winger Danny Armstrong scored in Dinamo Bucharest's 2-0 win over UTA Arad

'That era is gone. It is not coming back any time soon,' says Jo, dishing out tickets while fielding questions from visitors.

Football was strong under communist rule with star players tied to clubs and only allowed to leave for abroad at the behest of the government. Steaua was the team of the ministry of defence, Dinamo Bucharest was the team of the police. Both ruled the roost. Two years before Steaua won the Champions League, Dinamo lost in the semi-finals.

Now Steaua has been rent asunder. It is now called FCSB after a legal dispute over ownership of its name after a takeover by Gigi Becali. Dinamo have not won the title since 2006. Both seem to be haunted by old glories.

'I am Steaua,' says Jo. 'I always will be. My father was too. He said to me I had a choice: 'Support Steaua or sleep outside'.'

But Jo accepts that the best that can be hoped for is a minor renaissance in the national side.

'Club football at the highest level is simply about money and there is little of that here,' he says.

The verdict is more gloomy from Toni. With desultory glances towards Manchester City against Brighton playing out on multiple screens in the Half-Time Bar, the student says: 'The only team we have in European football this season is Universitatea (of Craiova). The others went out in qualifying. Steaua, for example, could not even qualify for the European Conference League. Universitatea is in that. That's where we are.'

There is no sneering from this Scot. 'Look at your country,' he says. 'Maybe a little bit better but nowhere near what it was.'

Dinamo Bucharest have not won the league for 20 years, but they have a passionate support

Ion, an older gentleman, interjects. 'It is a cabal now,' he says of European competition. 'Maybe good for the TV but only four or five teams outside of England can win it.'

But he adds: 'I am Dinamo. I still go. You will see what it means tomorrow.'

The Sunday game against UTA Arad is certainly compelling. There is a large crowd with an excellent atmosphere. But the cup tie last Wednesday against Chindia Targoviste was instructive for this observer.

It showcased what was still impressive about the Romanian game. It was possible, too, to have conversation with supporters as the cup is not taken too seriously at this stage and the crowd was only a few thousand.

The venue was the National Arena as the Dinamo Stadium is being rebuilt. The National Stadium is a wonderful arena, far better than anything we have to offer in Scotland. On Wednesday, as the rains thundered in Bucharest, the closed roof offered what seemed like a view of the stars but was, in fact, an array of lights peppering the modern protection from elements.

My accent invited conversation. 'Ah, a Scotsman,' muttered a companion in the splendid stand. 'Thank you for coming. It is good that Romanian football can be spoken about elsewhere.'

There was particular pleasure at my identity. 'Danny Armstrong is simply our hero,' says Nick, an engineer, who is at the game with his son and his friend Piti. 'He is the best player in the country and we will enjoy him while we can. Why does he not play for the national team?'

The answer to this is debated but there is no room for argument with Armstrong's impact on the Superliga since his move from Kilmarnock. 'It is not only goals and assists,' says Nick. 'He leads the team so well by his example. He is not in the team tonight because he is too important to risk in this fixture. If we are in trouble, he might come on but I don't foresee this.'

Gheorghe Hagi is among the Romanian legends celebrated at Bucharest's Muzeul Fotbalului

He is right. Dinamo win 5-2 and Armstrong remains on the bench. The player is thus fresh to give Mailsport an exclusive interview the next day. This is coming soon to a sports page near you but no spoiler alert is needed to reveal that the Scot is relishing his opportunity in the Romanian capital.

He is the fans' darling. And Dinamo, despite their recent lack of success, have a strong, impassioned support. 'This club has struggled and we have not won the league for 20 years,' says Piti. 'But there was even once a threat to our existence a few years ago but the fans pulled together.'

He points out that supporters would buy three tickets each for a game just to help Dinamo pay the bills. 'We put everything we could in. I know football is really just bread and circuses so success is not too important to me. But the existence of the club is. That's important.'

Dinamo stood for the opposition to the Ceausescu regime under communism. 'Steaua was run by Nicu, the son of Nicolae, the leader of the country. So it was regarded as the team of the regime and obviously it had strong links to the military. Dinamo was the team many dissenters backed.'

That was then. This is now. The team has strong designs on the title. 'With Danny we can do anything,' says Nick.

This sentiment was reinforced tonight. Armstrong walked on the pitch carrying his two-year-old daughter, Darby. He left to an ovation with minutes remaining, having scored a beautiful opener in their 2-0 victory. These are good days for the player and the fans who love him.

According to A Bola, the 21-year-old striker is beginning to attract interest from top European clubs. Several Premier League clubs, including Arsenal, have already shown an interest in Gustavo Varela.

Napoli are also following the Portuguese striker’s situation closely, while Barcelona have also been added to the list of interested clubs.

It is an impressive list of suitors for a player who came through the Sporting academy. That is hardly surprising, as he has been impressive at the start of this season.

Gustavo Varela has scored nine goals and provided one assist in nine Serie A matches. He is currently the league’s top scorer, ahead of Donyell Malen and his eight goals. The Portugal Under-21 international also scored twice in his only Coppa Italia match.

Monza are certainly aware they have hit the jackpot by signing Gustavo Varela for just £1.7m (€2m) this summer.

The Italian club are in a position of strength, with their striker’s contract running until June 2030. According to A Bola, the Serie A side are looking for a transfer fee in the region of £34m-£42.5m (€40m-€50m).

The player himself could also see his value rise if he is called up to the Portugal national team.

Jorge Jesus will announce his squad for the November international break on Friday, with a place in attack potentially available because of the situation surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo.

#1978. What Martin O'Neill told Kasper Hogh about Celtic goal drought after Besiktas

As German referee Sascha Stegemann sounded his full-time whistle, Martin O'Neill raised his right fist to the smoke-filled Glasgow sky.

Celtic's Europa League campaign was finally up and running courtesy of a frenetic 3-2 victory over Besiktas, the manager visibly relieved and triumphant in equal measure.

O'Neill usually heads straight up the tunnel after matches. Thursday evening was different. He instead made a beeline for his players before their customary walk round on the Celtic Park turf, embracing captain Callum McGregor and goalscorers Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran.

A turning point in Celtic's season? It's too early to say. But O'Neill knew for certain that failure to beat Besiktas would have rendered the remainder of Celtic's Europa League campaign meaningless. Now they have fresh hope and a platform for progress.

O'Neill insists they must build on their gutsy European victory.

"That is what we want to do, absolutely," O'Neill said. "From the European side, we have given ourselves a chance. We will have to go and win away from home and it will not be easy."

Thursday evening saw the manager make five changes to his lineup. Jordan Lotomba recorded his first start at right-back and Kasper Hogh, Sebastian Tounekti, and James Forrest made up a second string frontline.

From Forrest, O'Neill wanted experience and added defensive security. Hogh offered a focal point in attack and went off to a standing ovation in the 77th minute.

It marked his 15th Celtic appearance without a goal but the home crowd were appreciative of his work rate, as was O'Neill.

"I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did," O'Neill stated. "He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.

"I think Thursday night will be good for him. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

"Of course you want centre-forwards to score and of course centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him.

"I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game that he did really well."

Hogh, signed from Bodo/Glimt for a club record transfer fee in excess of £11 million during the summer transfer window, had no opportunities against Besiktas.

The Dane registered just one touch in the opposition penalty area and didn't have a single shot on goal.

Hogh is being starved of the service upon which he thrived at Bodo.

To that concern, O'Neill responded: "If they are going man for man and we have gone really, really low in terms of going close to the goalkeeper then the next one in if you are dinking it in is where a centre-forward has to play.

"If it is a decent ball in then he has to hold it up because he should be first. If it is in the air and he has to fight for it then it is difficult. But if you dink it in for him then you can start from there."

"Centre-forwards need a goal," O'Neill continued. "But that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence. I don’t know what side we will play on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League remember.

"He will get a confidence boost from Thursday night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal."

Hogh needn't have to worry about goals if Duran maintains his apex form. The Colombian couldn't have been more influential after coming off the bench against Besiktas, netting a crucial brace to give Celtic all three points.

First, Duran latched on to Osmand's reverse pass, rounding opposition goalkeeper Alexander Nubel and slotting into an empty net. He then brilliantly controlled Kieran Tierney's wayward shot, this time beating Nubel from six yards out.

"At this minute, he is on fire," O'Neill said of Duran. "He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left for his other club. But centre-forward is where he is dynamic."

When Duran plays through the middle, Hogh is often sacrificed. Conversely, Hogh starting usually sees Duran shifted to the right flank. For O'Neill, it's onerous finding the perfect balance.

"We made five changes on Thursday night because it was necessary," he explained. "The boys who came on were always going to come on after 60 minutes.

"You can’t just plan things like this. Somebody might pick up an injury. Things change during the course of the game. But the plan before it was for these lads to go on. We were always going to make the changes.

"It was necessary if we wanted a bit more gusto in the side and a bit more playing in behind. That gave the opportunity for Duran to weave a bit of magic."

Focus rightly lay on Celtic's attacking play after Thursday. Yet their defence was equally pivotal, limiting Besiktas to few opportunities of note.

Beyond a penalty and the resulting rebound, from which they scored, Vincenzo Italiano's side offered little in the way of forward penetration, struggling to break down Celtic's organised structure. It took a long-range effort from Orkun Kokcu to score their second of the evening.

"It was really pleasing and really important," O'Neill said of his team's defending. "We conceded some ground in the game which was to be expected, but I thought defensively we were really, really strong.

"When corners came in we dealt with them and we dealt with second balls as well after it was played out. The back four was terrific. Lotomba did well until he conceded the penalty."

Central defender Cameron Carter-Vickers had one of his better displays. The American made nine clearances and won all but one of his five duels. Accurate on the ball too, Carter-Vickers brought an air of stability to the backline.

He recovered ably from his performance against Falkirk last weekend, when his meek clearance led directly to Ethan Ross' opener. Carter-Vickers came off in the latter stages with a hamstring complaint, but O'Neill thinks he had a point to prove.

"It looked that way," said the Celtic boss. "I thought he was very strong. He was complaining about his hamstrings being very tight at half-time and I thought we would give him another 15 minutes.

"Of course, the game changed in that time and we were chasing the game from behind. But the lads who came on in the forward positions were always going to come on. James Forrest was never going to last the whole game.

"I thought he was outstanding, an absolute credit to the football club with what he did for us. Even defensively. Everybody worked so hard. It was really pleasing."

The key for Celtic and O'Neill is building on Thursday's thrilling victory. As the manager knows all too well, it'll count for nothing if Kilmarnock, St Mirren, and Torreense aren't beaten in the coming weeks.
