#1906. The Man Utd change Michael Carrick must make against Aston Villa to keep his job

With JJ Gabriel almost out the door at Old Trafford Manchester United, and Michael Carrick will now be tempted to pin all their hopes on another emerging star in Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old has played himself into first-team contention after a dazzling display off the bench in Tuesday’s comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League.

While it was Bruno Fernandes’ penalty that sparked the revival and Matheus Cunha’s brace that got them over the line, Lacey’s fearless cameo on the right was the catalyst for change.

Even the perennially reserved Michael Carrick couldn’t hide his delight over the performance, noting the teenager has ‘that bit of mischief’ in his locker that troubled Roma for the final 15 minutes of the game. Lacey ended the contest playing in defence after Cunha’s red card with Carrick jokingly christening him his new right-back.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Lacey’s sharp, perfectly-weighted passing enabled United to get up the pitch with real intent – seldom seen this season. He completed every one of his attempted passes and completed all but one of his duels. Operating in tight spaces just in front of the touchline, his first touches and clever exchanges were on point from the moment he came on. His pass for Cunha’s winner couldn’t have been placed better.

It has been a long time coming for Lacey. Injuries shelved tentative plans for him to make his debut at 16 under Erik ten Hag in 2023 and it was a tough road back from those issues that threatened to halt his progress.

‘Everybody in the world knows about Shea Lacey,’ United’s former Under-21 manager Travis Binnion said last year. ‘So he needs a little bit of fortune, he needs to be patient with himself and everybody else needs to be really patient with him.’ That patience could now be about to pay off.

Whether Tuesday’s win was a turning point or another false dawn for United remains to be seen. Jose Mourinho and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer led United to delirium-inducing comeback victories over Newcastle United in Atalanta with identical scorelines when the pressure was mounting on their shoulders. Both were gone shortly after.

But with Carrick’s back against the wall, there is the opportunity to roll the dice with Lacey. The Liverpool-born talent thumped home a wonderful strike in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton but has seen just 31 minutes of action off the bench since. Excluding the second-half performance against Roma, United’s attack has lacked any verve or real invention. A change is needed and Lacey will feel this is his chance.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It was on the right where he caused damage midweek with Amad Diallo making way for him after 75 minutes. It had been another disappointing evening for the Ivory Coast international who spurned huge opportunities against Chelsea four days earlier.

Since forcing his way back into the side under Erik ten Hag, Amad has been looked upon as United’s most naturally talented winger. But his goal and assist return has fallen woefully short of expectations. He is now approaching one year without a goal, last finding the back of the net in the 4-4 draw with Bournemouth on 15 December. In that time, he has provided two assists – one on the final day of last season against Brighton and the other for Joshua Zirkzee’s consolation goal in the 4-1 humiliation in Como two weeks ago.

His haul of 14 goals during his magnificent campaign with Sunderland in the 2022-23 season is a distant memory. A hat-trick against Southampton in January 2025 helped him to an impressive haul of 11 goals and 10 assists in his first full campaign back in Manchester but seven goal involvements in 40 appearances since the start of the 2025-26 campaign is not good enough.

Wayne Rooney alluded to Amad’s problem midweek and made his case for Lacey getting the nod.

‘Amad does some really good things, but it’s that end product, that is what takes you to the next level,’ he told Amazon Prime. ‘And the glimpses of what I’ve seen from Lacey when he has come on…he has got something in there, that little touch and little pass which United needed to get them over the line in this game.’

The win over Roma has shifted a few clouds amid the gloom hanging over Old Trafford and Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa now looks a more inviting environment for Carrick to make the change and put his faith in Lacey.

#1905. Estrela Amadora vs Benfica - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 06 Nov 2026 11:31, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 11:44

Returning to league action after a midweek Europa League fixture, Benfica make the short trip across Lisbon to face Estrela Amadora in the sides' 11th Primeira Liga meeting.

The Tricolours' losing streak stretched to four matches last week as they suffered a 2-1 defeat to Moreirense, while Marco Silva's side recorded their seventh consecutive victory in all competitions after overcoming Lech Poznan 3-1 on Thursday evening.

Estrela Amadora will be eager to end their poor run of form, which has seen them slip out of the top six and drop to 12th in the table following four consecutive defeats against Academico Viseu, Arouca, Casa Pia and, most recently, Moreirense.

However, Pepa's side did at least end a three-game run without scoring in their latest outing, with Lovro Zvonarek finding the net shortly before the hour mark.

Amid their struggles in the league, which have seen them go five matches without a victory in the Primeira Liga, Estrela did manage to secure progression to the next round of the Taca de Portugal, although they were made to work considerably harder than expected.

Despite being strong favourites to overcome fourth-tier Fazendense, the Tricolours were still level heading into the final 10 minutes before Tom Moustier scored his second goal of the game five minutes from time to prevent a potential cup upset.

Pepa's men went unbeaten across their opening six league fixtures, picking up impressive results against Sporting Lisbon and Braga, but they now face one of the toughest challenges in Portuguese football as they prepare to welcome Benfica.

That challenge comes in the form of an Eagles side who make the short journey to Amadora with seven consecutive victories in all competitions behind them.

Since suffering a 3-1 defeat to Porto in the league, Silva's men have enjoyed an impressive run of results, thrashing Celtic in the Europa League, progressing comfortably in the cup and reducing the gap to the league leaders to five points.

Benfica have scored 20 goals across their last seven matches, finding the net at least four times on three occasions during that run.

Their attacking performances have also helped them record an 80% win rate in the Primeira Liga, with no side scoring more than their 27 goals, while only four teams have conceded fewer than their eight.

In the Europa League, Benfica made it four wins from four on Thursday evening, with goals from Rafa Silva, Gianluca Prestianni and Georgiy Sudakov securing a 3-1 victory over Lech Poznan and sending the Eagles to the top of the league-phase table.

Since Estrela secured promotion from Liga Portugal 2 in 2022-23, despite only being founded six years ago, the two sides have met regularly, but the Tricolours have ended up losing all nine encounters.

Estrela Amadora should be able to name an unchanged starting XI from the side that lost to Moreirense last weekend, although they remain without Robinho and Jeremy Arevalo.

Ianis Stoica is the club's leading scorer with four goals but has not found the net since September.

Despite his recent drought, the Romanian is expected to retain his place in the starting line-up.

Vangelis Pavlidis leads the Primeira Liga scoring charts with 10 goals in 10 appearances and, despite being an unused substitute in Benfica's most recent European fixture, is expected to return to the starting XI for this encounter.

Silva has regularly rotated goalkeepers Anatoliy Trubin and Samuel Soares throughout the campaign, with the former featuring in midweek but not in the league last weekend, although the Benfica boss could stick with the Ukrainian between the posts on Sunday

The former Hull City, Everton and Fulham manager will, however, be unable to call upon ex-Tottenham defender Clement Lenglet or Leandro Barreiro.

Estrela Amadora possible starting lineup:

Linck; Scholze, L. Patrick, Lekovic, Davin; Jansson, Serra; Marcus, Zvonarek, Stoica; Antonetti

Soares; Bah, Araujo, Circati, Dahl; Sudakov, Palhinha; Silva, Prestianni, Schjelderup; Pavlidis

With one of Europe's most prolific attacking sides facing a team that have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last 12 matches, we expect Benfica to have plenty of opportunities to find the net.

The Eagles have lost just once this season, and we back Silva's men to extend their winning run to eight matches on Sunday and secure a second 3-1 victory in the space of four days.

Arsenal have been closely tracking the progress of Monza star Gustavo Varela are ‘one of the first clubs to enquire’ about a possible transfer deal for the forward, according to reports in Portugal.

Varela was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and moved to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

Monza are languishing down in 18th place in the table, with only two wins to their name, in what has been a difficult start to life on their return to Serie A.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring nine goals in his opening nine appearances, and his barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

It’s claimed Arsenal are among a host of Premier League clubs to have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

The reigning English champions are said to be in the market for a striker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres badly struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

The report adds that Monza have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m). That this sum is likely to rise again if Jorge Jesus hands the attacker his first senior Portugal call-up on Friday.

‘I didn’t expect to start off so strong,’ Varela recently said of his lightning start in Italian football.

Rumours over potential attacking additions at Arsenal will continue as long as Gyokeres’ performances fail to improve in north London.

The Sweden international has made just one start in the Premier League season and is still yet to find the net in the English top flight, with Mikel Arteta favouring Kai Havertz as the focal point of his attack.

However, Gyokeres will have done his chances no harm whatsoever with a strong display in the Champions League on Wednesday night as he scored and assisted in a 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague.

Facing the media shortly after the final whistle in Prague, Arteta heaped praise on Gyokeres’ showing, applauding his ‘connection’ with his team-mates.

‘I thought he was really good. It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

#1898. Stafford Rangers vs Grimsby Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 06 Nov 2026 11:31

Grimsby Town make the trip to Stafford Rangers on Sunday afternoon looking to avoid one of the biggest upsets in recent FA Cup history.

While the visitors to Marston Road sit in sixth place in the League Two table, Stafford Rangers are second in the Northern Premier League West Division, a league in the eighth tier of English football.

When Stafford Rangers took to the pitch for their FA Cup extra preliminary round tie against Tividale on August 8, the aim was to come through two matches to make the first qualifying round, maybe go one step further and earn a tie with a National League North or South club.

Six rounds and two replays later, Stafford Rangers are in the first round preparing to welcome EFL opposition to Marston Road, dreaming of causing another major upset in the competition.

Graham Deakin's side have already defeated the likes of National League North high-flyers Hereford FC and National League strugglers Gateshead, the latter being thrashed 5-0 in a one-sided replay after a 1-1 draw in the North-East.

Their promotion campaign in the Northern Premier League West Division remains their priority. They sit in second place behind Bootle, trailing by seven points with a match in hand.

Nevertheless, 20 years on from a 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion in the FA Cup second round, the Boro have the opportunity to take on a team sitting 89 places above them in the English football pyramid.

David Artell will feel that Grimsby have returned to form at the right time as they look to avoid making unwanted headlines on Sunday.

A seven-match winless streak in all competitions has been followed by successive wins over Gillingham and York City.

The Mariners scored nine goals in the process, leaving them with the joint-third best attacking record in League Two after 14 matches.

Although their last away game ended in a 4-1 win at Gillingham, it marked their first away success in the fourth tier this season.

Grimsby reached the fourth round of the 2025-26 FA Cup before losing 1-0 at home to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Stafford Rangers form (all competitions):

Stafford Rangers will be without defender Mitch Clarke, who will be sidelined for the foreseeable future with an injury sustained against Lower Breck last weekend. Derby County youngster Luke Banks has been signed to strengthen the central-defensive ranks.

Deakin made alterations for Wednesday's 1-0 win at Congleton, giving the manager food for thought for this contest.

Ellis Horan, who is eligible due to the recently-changed rules over players representing two clubs in the same FA Cup campaign, has scored in three successive games.

Given the finances involved, Artell may avoid the temptation to make many alterations to his Grimsby XI.

Justin Amaluzor may be given an opportunity on the flank, while Josh Andrews could be provided with a rare start in attack to hand a rest to veteran Andy Cook.

Barring any fresh issues, Reece Staunton is the only injury absentee.

Stafford Rangers possible starting lineup:

Phillips; Gomes, Dunne, Burns, Tonks, Bakkor, Webster, Horan, Washington, Navarro, Efunnuga

Pym; Rodgers, Kacurri, McJannet; Foulkes, Turi, Walker, Vernam; Green; Morgan, Andrews

Stafford Rangers have already shown at Marston Road this season that they can rise to the occasion in the FA Cup. However, despite their previous wins against higher-league opposition in recent months, we can only see Grimsby showing their class in this contest.

#1897. Former Man Utd chairman slams owners after controversial Avram Glazer comments

Former Manchester United chairman Martin Edwards expects supporters to be furious with Avram Glazer’s comments on the club and has accused the owners of getting their priorities wrong.

The Athletic report that Glazer made a controversial point while speaking to financiers at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London in September.

One of the owners of the Red Devils compared Manchester United to the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys as a brand that will remain commercially successful irrespective of how well they are performing on the pitch.

Edwards, who was chairman of Manchester United from 1980-2003, expects fans to react badly to that sentiment and has encouraged the current owners to train all their focus on improving the team.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘I heard that this morning and I thought “By Jove, what’s the reaction going to be from the supporters?” Supporters don’t want to hear that!’ Edwards said on talkSPORT.

‘Supporters want to hear that you’re winning trophies. They’re not interested in profits or dividends or what people are taking out of the club. They want the club to be successful, they want the best players, they’d rather be spending money on the team than on the new stadium.’

Edwards accepts that running a club the size of Manchester United is a tricky business and owners must satisfy various stakeholders, but he feels the balance is currently off.

‘When I was running United, I always felt I had three responsibilities, really,’ he said. ‘One: in those days we were still developing the ground, so I had to build the ground and develop the ground. Look after the team, which is always the most important. But also, because we were public we had to pay dividends and keep the shareholders happy.

‘It’s a balance. Running a football club is a complete balance, from top to balance. It’s a question of whether you get it right or wrong.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He added: ‘I think it’s quite clear, in my eyes, that the team is the most important element at the moment. You’ve got to get the team right and forget new stadiums if you’re not going to fill them. Get the team winning again and get the supporters behind you. We’re not a united front at the moment.’

The landscape of top flight football has changed considerably since Edwards was in charge at Manchester United and he believes it has not all been for the better.

‘You’ve got owners now who don’t attend games. They put somebody in charge, whatever else,’ he said. ‘Existing owners now, they wouldn’t know who’s in the team.

‘It’s become big business and what you can get out of it. The game has changed and for the older ones of us it’s disappointing, really, the direction it’s gone.’

Looking back to the start of Manchester United’s decline as a title-challenging force in the Premier League, Edwards suggests it was the loss of Alex Ferguson and CEO David Gill in 2013 and Ed Woodward being named as Gill’s replacement.

‘Once Alec and David Gill decided to leave in 2013, that was a huge blow to the club and they’ve never really recovered from that,’ he said.

‘If you wanted to be critical you’d say right from the beginning when they replaced David Gill, they replaced him with not a football man, but a merchant banker.

‘If you’ve got the top of the football chain who’s not converse with football, that does make it difficult. I think that once the mistakes start, they multiply.

‘Recruitment has been a big problem. Look at the players they’ve bought, some of them haven’t been up to the standard. Generally it snowballs. That’s been the problem.

‘Also, have United spent enough money to be able to compete at the top? Manchester City have had a huge advantage in the short-term because they haven’t been sticking to the rules and other people have. That’s given them a huge advantage, so we probably couldn’t have competed with them, but we could certainly have competed with Liverpool and Arsenal and whatever else.’

#1896. Nothing personal says England coach Thomas Tuchel as he overlooks Cole Palmer

The Chelesa playmaker has been left out of the group to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this month, having pulled out of the last squad through injury.

But there are first call-ups for midfielders Josh King and Jobe Bellingham, the brother of England talisman Jude, whilst the Leeds United pair of James Trafford and Dominic Calvert-Lewin have been retained.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Phil Foden has already learnt the high bar Tuchel has for his squad, and Palmer appears to be the latest star name in his bad books.

But the German insists it is not the case.

“I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception,” said Tuchel despite his pointed comments during the last camp about how many internationals Palmer had been unavailable for.

“I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary.

“If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal, and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country. But the competition is on, and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.

“The door is always open, but nothing has changed.”

Palmer was one of five withdrawals ahead of the last camp, along with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford. Of them, only Arsenal midfielder Rice is in the current squad.

Palmer has only won five caps since scoring in the 2024 European Championship final.

The younger Bellingham has never played in the Premier League after leaving Sunderland for Borussia Dortmund two summers ago but has established himself as an important player in the Bundesliga.

He and King have benefited from the absence through injury of Alex Scott, and the fact Mainoo only returned to Manchester United's starting XI on Tuesday.

Dean Henderson returns after injury, along with former Leeds loanees Djed Spence and Ben White.

White made himself unavailable following the 2022 World Cup after a reported disagreement with Gareth Southgate's No 2 Steve Holland.

He made himself available once Tuchel took over, and made his return as a 69th-minute substitute against Uruguay in March.

He was booed onto the field that night, and even scoring England's goal in a 1-1 draw did not win over the Wembley crowd.

"We were not happy about this," said Tuchel. "We could understand the disappointment of the fans with what happened before but I think this is expressed now and this should be a closed book.

“I think everyone could see the investment of Ben, the quality of Ben and how he presented himself in the March camp before the World Cup.

“He did excellently, scored for us and then I think he committed a foul and we conceded.

“It was very eventful, not so easy to come back. When I speak to him, I always feel the hunger to come back, the excitement.

“He is the standout player for Arsenal in a position (right-back) where we struggle with injuries somehow and we have a lot of changes.

“Trevoh Chalobah is not in camp so that makes maybe Jarell Quansah half a full-back and half a centre-back in camp and gives Ben the opportunity to impose himself again.

“He deserves to open a new chapter, he deserves positive feedback from the crowd.

“We want everyone to be supported. This is what helps the team.”

England play at home to Croatia on Thursday, and are in Madrid the following Sunday for their final group match of the competition.

SQUAD: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Dean Henderson (Crystal Palace); Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal); Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal); Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea).

#1895. Jack Grealish left at home AGAIN for Everton's clash with Newcastle... but boss David Moyes says there IS a way back for on-loan winger

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 09:50 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 17:45 EDT, 2 November 2026

Jack Grealish was not fit enough to feature for Everton at Newcastle on Monday night after he missed training following a night out last week.

The 31-year-old was dropped for Thursday’s 3-1 Carabao Cup win at home to Newcastle following a ‘breach of club discipline’.

Grealish had failed to show for Monday’s session and it is understood staff struggled to make contact with the winger.

But despite returning to training, the Manchester City loanee was left behind on Merseyside yesterday after it was decided he was still not ready to play. In his absence, the Toffees won 1-0. Everton manager Moyes said after the game: ‘He’s just not available yet.’

Asked if the situation was repairable, the Scot paused, and added: ‘Of course it is.’

Grealish had made four successive starts before he missed Everton’s 2-0 defeat by Arsenal on October 24 due to illness.

He will be given this week to build fitness ahead of Friday’s visit of Coventry.

Jack Grealish missed Everton's Premier League win over Newcastle on Monday night

Daily Mail Sport understands Grealish, 31, is building fitness after being left out of David Moyes's squad for their Carabao Cup tie with the Magpies last week

It is thought Moyes had reservations about re-signing Grealish this summer after similar issues last season. He said he was not sure if the player would be available on Friday.

Moyes backed the 'club decision' following the 3-1 victory, which saw the Toffees advance to the quarter-finals.

'You probably know I’m not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don’t want to speak too much about,' Moyes said on Thursday.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job.

'It’s a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them, the players need to keep at it and we are not accepting any excuses. There’s a humility about us tonight.'

Grealish has made seven appearances since rejoining Everton for a second season-long loan spell in the summer.

‘Are Arsenal at a high enough level now that William Saliba would turn down Real Madrid if they came in for him?’ Gallas told SeatPick.

‘I know a lot of people will be mad about what I’m going to say right now but if we are talking about the history of both clubs, Real Madrid and Arsenal, then Real Madrid is Real Madrid. They are on a different level.’

‘For me, even if their performances at the moment are not the best, and even if they haven’t won the biggest trophies recently, Madrid is Madrid, and I’m telling you, any player who has the opportunity to go to Madrid, they will try to go there, and you can’t blame them. #1892. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 06 Nov 2026 11:43, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:46

Ipswich Town play host to Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon looking for the win that could catapult them into the top half of the Premier League table.

While the Tractor Boys start the next batch of fixtures in 14th position, the Cherries are in eighth place after three successive victories in the top flight.

With Ipswich having failed to win in three Premier League matches, Gary O'Neil may feel that an opportunity has been missed.

As well as there being frustration after a 3-2 defeat at Manchester City, the Tractor Boys have only earned draws against Nottingham Forest and Hull City respectively.

However, Ipswich came from behind to secure a share of the spoils in both contests, keeping the club within touching distance of the top six.

Although O'Neil will perhaps be prioritising staying at least four points clear of the relegation zone, Ipswich currently possess the joint-fourth best attacking record in the division with 14 goals.

Furthermore, their only defeat at Portman Road this season has come against Liverpool, Ipswich earning five points from the other fixtures versus Sunderland, Fulham and Nottingham Forest.

Nevertheless, O'Neil welcomes one of his former clubs to East Anglia with Bournemouth one of the form teams in Europe.

Since a 5-1 defeat at Chelsea on October 10, Marco Rose's side have won seven games in a row across three different competitions.

A total of 19 goals have been netted during that period, while the only goal that they have conceded came in the 3-1 win at Sparta Prague in the Europa League on Thursday.

Given Bournemouth's relatively-small squad, Rose will not be getting carried away with his team's form, but the South-coast outfit are one game away from a near-perfect return during a run of nine matches in less than a month.

Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds United have been defeated in succession in the top flight. However, the success at Old Trafford remains their only away win in the Premier League in four games.

While O'Neil is unlikely to make many changes to his Ipswich XI, Azor Matusiwa, Daizen Maeda and Jack Clarke are all alternatives in midfield and the final third.

#1891. Premier League star sparks major police operation after being spotted with a bow and arrows

Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic sparked a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows near a reservoir in Northumberland.

Dedic, who joined Newcastle in a £30 million deal from Benfica in the summer, was reported by a member of the public who saw him and a friend walking with the weapon near the small village of Harlow Hill.

According to the Daily Mail, police dispatched several vehicles to the area, including some that were armed response units.

Dedic and his friend were stopped by police before officers searched a car and seized the bow and arrows.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

After their investigation, officers deemed that there was no threat to the public, although enquiries are ongoing.

Dedic and his friend are said to have fired some arrows while out in the countryside, although it has not been determined what they were aiming at.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

‘Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.’

The Daily Mail adds that Dedic will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident.

#1889. Ryan Giggs sends Max Dowman message to JJ Gabriel over Manchester United exit

Ryan Giggs has urged JJ Gabriel to reconsider his decision to leave Manchester United and believes the 16-year-old should follow Max Dowman’s pathway at Arsenal.

Gabriel, who turned 16 last month, informed United of his desire to leave Old Trafford in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, however, he has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

Gabriel’s entourage are understood to have been unhappy with his first-team integration at United and wanted him to feature in a Champions League fixture against Sabah FK, as well as in a Carabao Cup tie against Brighton in September.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Giggs, meanwhile, also began his career as a highly rated young prospect in United’s academy but did not make his first-team debut until the age of 17 under Sir Alex Ferguson.

The 52-year-old went on to become the most decorated player in English football history as he won 34 trophies during his 24-year career with United.

When asked about Gabriel’s situation in a conversation with Rio Ferdinand, Giggs stressed the importance of patience and believes Dowman, who was handed his Arsenal debut at 15 years and 235 days old in August 2025, is going through the correct development process under Mikel Arteta.

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. #1888. Why Unai Emery is right to turn down Manchester United and stick with Aston Villa

It’s a great quirk of Premier League scheduling that Manchester United welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford this weekend, after a week in which Jamie Carragher’s suggestion that Villa manager Unai Emery would jump at the chance to move to United prompted a legal threat from the midlands club, an apology from the outspoken pundit and an announcement late on Wednesday that Emery and his bosses had ‘positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club’.

A new contract is reportedly imminent for the Spaniard, and who could possibly blame Emery for sticking around at a club that have repeatedly backed him, given him more control than he’ll have anywhere else and whose fans worship him for delivering their first trophy in 30 years last season.

The alternative? Joining a constant catastrophe that everyone agrees needs far more than just a new manager to put back together.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

While Emery is going nowhere, the whole affair does raise questions about football’s food chain, something which definitely does exist but is clearly going through some changes right now.

Managers will always believe they are the right person to take a once great club and bring back the glory days, and being the one to do so is an intoxicating idea.

But Emery has been here before and was burned by his experience at Arsenal where a collection of expensive failed transfers and unmotivated senior players gave him the worst possible platform to build from. Sound familiar?

All roads still lead to Real Madrid for players but the money involved in Premier League football means simply being a relatively successful English club puts you closer to the top of the chain than ever before, and given United’s penchant for finding new lows every season, a move from Villa north to Manchester is at best a sideways move these days – just ask Youri Tielemans.

Also, given the relative state of flux that many of the ‘big six’ find themselves in these days, there’s an opportunity for Emery and Villa to elbow their way in and become a more established fixture towards the top of the league.

Select your team for football news tailored to you Close

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United are joined by Spurs in their ability to self-implode, Chelsea are chaotic at the best of times, Liverpool are still just about managing the transition to a Jurgen Klopp-less existence and Manchester City are unlikely to be challenging for titles in the near future, depending on impending sanctions.

Only Arsenal are properly set up for consistent success, and Villa clearly believe trusting in Emery is the best way to eventually get themselves into the title conversation.

There are pitfalls to their approach – if Emery does someday get his head turned by a massive paycheck in Saudi Arabia or Real Madrid do come calling, he may still move on and leave the club as a ship without a sail, which is why clubs like Brighton and Brentford treat their managers as cogs in a well-oiled system.

United fans had some temporary relief midweek with their emotional comeback against Roma in the Champions League and may well go into the international break feeling good if they manage to squeeze out a win on Sunday, but regardless of the result, Emery is in the right place.

#1887. Manchester United manager search takes major twist as new Michael Carrick details emerge

Didier Deschamps has reportedly turned down an approach over the Manchester United manager’s job, as more details emerge over the future of Michael Carrick.

Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been subject to severe scrutiny for several weeks now following a miserable eight-game winless run across all competitions that was the club’s worst since the 1988/89 season.

Such a dire sequence was only snapped on Tuesday night as Man Utd staged an incredible turnaround following an abysmal first half to beat depleted Roma 3-2 at home in the Champions League, though it remains to be seen how much respite that offered their beleaguered head coach.

Sky Sports report that there remains support for Carrick within the United hierarchy, who have been said to be split on a potential replacement amid strong links to the likes of former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann.

However, Sunday’s visit of Aston Villa to Old Trafford is likely to prove crucial before another review of the situation, with United having won just one of their opening nine games in the Premier League this term - at home to newly-promoted Ipswich back in August - as they go into the final weekend before the November international break sitting 17th in the table and outside of the relegation zone on goal difference only.

Villa are led by Unai Emery, who has also been linked with United but is expected now to sign a new long-term contract at Villa Park.

In a shock further twist to the saga, it was initially claimed in France on Thursday that Deschamps had been approached about potentially succeeding Carrick.

The 58-year-old is currently out of work after his successful 14-year spell in charge of the French national team - which included several major finals and one World Cup triumph - ended following the summer tournament, when he stood down after the expiration of his contract and was replaced by Zinedine Zidane.

However, it has since been reported by multiple outlets that Deschamps has indicated that he would have no interest in taking the United job as things stand, instead preferring to wait to likely return to football next summer.

United are not believed to be keen to appoint another interim manager if they do decide to part ways with Carrick, who was appointed to the full-time job in the summer on the strength of his success as a caretaker over the second half of last season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January.

#1886. Man United transfer news: Barcelona eye cut-price January swoop for Lisandro Martinez

By Axel Clody | 06 Nov 2026 11:52

Barcelona are on the hunt for a centre-back for the next winter transfer window and Lisandro Martinez appears to be a realistic option.

Barcelona are in better financial health, as their last summer transfer window showed. The Catalan club invested £156.5m (€184m) to sign players including Rodri and Anthony Gordon. However, they have very little room for manoeuvre under the strict financial rules imposed by La Liga.

Without a major departure, Barcelona will not be able to invest heavily in a centre-back in the next winter window. That could hamper the club’s hierarchy in their search, with a shortlist of four names having been revealed: Josko Gvardiol, Natan, Lisandro Martinez and Alessandro Bastoni.

Raphinha’s contract extension, whose salary will be redistributed to free up space in the current season’s wage bill, will create a small additional budget.

However, Barcelona ‘could not cover both the transfer fee and the share of the wage bill corresponding to a top-level player’, according to Sport.

A loan solution appears, but it is not really in line with what the Spanish champions are looking for. They want to sign an experienced centre-back who can make an immediate impact.

No club therefore has an interest in loaning out a player of that standard, unless a mandatory option to buy is included.

Faced with the complexity of such a move, the option of Lisandro Martinez appears realistic and could suit all parties.

The Argentine is approaching the end of his Manchester United contract and is not set to extend his stay. Barcelona and Manchester United could therefore negotiate a transfer for an affordable fee.

The 28-year-old could also sign a contract on a low salary until the end of the season, to ease his arrival in January, before being compensated with higher payments in the following seasons, Sport points out. It would be a good deal from a financial point of view.

It remains to be seen whether it is feasible and whether Hansi Flick will approve this defensive reinforcement. It should be noted that the German manager was not convinced by Alessandro Bastoni last summer.

#1885. Newcastle look like a team bereft of energy and inspiration under Matthias Jaissle - as Everton continue to thrive without Jack Grealish after another impressive victory, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 17:16 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EDT, 2 November 2026

Jack Grealish was pictured enjoying a cracking night out in Newcastle last year. Here, his Everton team-mates had just as good a time, albeit in a far more sober state.

The Manchester City loanee was left at home after last week’s ‘breach of club discipline’. At least, home is where the club hoped he would be.

And, if he was, Grealish would have watched Everton record a deserved win. He might even have raised a toast, so accomplished an away performance was this.

David Moyes had dropped the winger for last Thursday’s 3-1 win over Newcastle in the Carabao Cup after he missed training following another alleged night on the town. And again, without him, they were too good for Matthias Jaissle’s sorry and directionless Newcastle.

It is the Toon Army, rather, in need of a bender right now. They really aren’t very good - no shots on target before injury-time - and it is remarkable to think they would have gone seventh with victory. That position is now occupied by Everton, who were more skilful and more savvy from start to finish and won thanks to Thierno Barry’s goal just after the break. The scoreline was not a reflection of their superiority.

Jaissle said: ‘We were not brave enough to break the line and play on the ground. We saw it in training, but there was almost nothing to see from these aspects in the game.

Everton, who were more skilful and more savvy from start to finish, won thanks to Thierno Barry’s goal just after the break

Jaissle’s promise has been a team who hunt in packs, yet they were hiding en mass here

‘We have a clear identity of how we want to play - to bring the opposition in stressful situations high in the pitch. We spoke about creating one-on-one situations. The plan was not to play the long balls.’

The opening half hour had been a side-show in two managers betraying varying degrees of frustration. Jaissle buried his fist in his palm every time Everton played through his team at will. And Moyes muttered expletives when his side were unable to take advantage. It was clear he sensed this was there to be won. It was less clear how they would achieve that when Barry was swiping at fresh air six yards from goal.

Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 4; Dedic 4, Schar 5, Burn 5, Hall 5; Gonzalez 4 (Steur 64, 6), Joelinton 4 (Ramsey 76, 5); Elanga 4 (Murphy 76, 5) Willock 4 (Wissa 64, 5), Barnes 5; Osula 4.

Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; O’Brien 7, Tarkowski 7, Branthwaite 7, Mykolenko 7; Garner 7, Armstrong 7; Rohl 6, DEWSBURY-HALL 8, George 6; Barry 7.

By the 28th minute, the home fans were booing after yet another aimless long ball. Vertical football, Jaissle has called it, getting the ball forward quickly. Yet more boos on the whistle for half-time told you the locals fear they are going backwards. Everton’s Harrison Armstrong, the half’s brightest midfielder, had only just swiped wide from 12 yards when he should have scored, and that would have been deserved.

The Toon Army were soon cheering, when a fella in jeans kicked a ball through a hole to win a trip to Las Vegas. It was the first effort on target by anyone on the field all evening. Newcastle’s first-half woe was summed up by one free-kick, worked short, that was then chipped straight out of play by Amar Dedic. Jaissle shot to his dugout to watch a replay of what had gone wrong - someone should have told him such footage could not be re-shown pre watershed.

The first effort on target brought the first goal in the 49th minute, and it was no surprise when it came Everton’s way. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall played the sort of pass of which Newcastle were seemingly incapable - low, incisive and accurate - and that set Tyrique George away. His shot was not particularly hard, but then Lukas Hornicek’s attempt to save it was not particularly convincing. As the ball squirmed through his grasp, Barry was quickest to follow up for a tap-in. Newcastle appealed offsides against both George and the scorer, but the truth was that Everton’s players were just sharper in every phase. The time afforded to the excellent Dewsbury-Hall to pick that pass was also a scandal.

Jaissle’s promise has been a team who hunt in packs. They were hiding en mass here. The head coach looked to his bench and called for the popular midfielder Sean Steur. The Dutch teenager’s popularity has been enhanced by him not being in the side of late. The cheer for his introduction, as replacement for the leaden-booted Nico Gonzalez, was almost as big as for the sharp-shooter in Levi’s.

Immediately, Steur impacted. From one smart pass to Harvey Barnes the winger crossed and Anthony Elanga almost stole in to score at the far post. The Geordies have been right to call for his involvement in a team so void of inspiration and positive energy.

It was not long, however, before a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ emerged from the Gallowgate End, and that is never a good sign. Substitute Jacob Ramsey was then sent off for a second booking to compound the home misery.

Meanwhile, the fan bound for Vegas was probably checking for the next flight.

#1883. Tottenham 'retain clause' in Harry Kane contract after Ballon d'Or win and new Bayern Munich deal

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham's agreement with Bayern Munich over Harry Kane remains in place, despite the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner signing a new contract.

After weeks of speculation, it was announced on Thursday that Kane has committed his future to Bayern until the summer of 2029 and reportedly becoming the highest-paid player in Europe by base salary.

Kane's new deal comes hot on the heels of winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or award over Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, though he is now targeting more team success with the Bundesliga giants.

“We signed the contract yesterday, but the decision was made quite a long time ago," he said. "As I’ve said before, I know I’m part of a great team, that we’re competing for the Champions League and for every title.

"It’s important for me to be somewhere where I can improve. There’s no doubt about that here. My family is happy that we can stay here – overall, everyone’s happy.”

While Kane is happy and settled in Germany, a return to England with Tottenham at some point in the future has not completely ruled out following the new contract - even if there is currently no suggestion of this scenario materialising.

Spurs have confirmed that as part of Kane's move to Bayern in 2023, they negotiated a clause allowing them to match any bid made for the striker.

However, it was recently suggested by transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano that Bayern were looking at removing such clause which would have all-but ruled out a return to the Premier League for Kane.

Now, Telegraph Sport have reported that Spurs retained their first-option matching rights for the England captain.

As such, should Bayern - who are said to currently view Kane as “untouchable” - agree to sell the striker before his new contract expires, Tottenham would have to decide whether to match the bid in order to give the striker a decision to make.

Arsenal should be wary of selling Viktor Gyokeres in the January transfer window, according to former Gunners striker Jeremie Aliadiere.

But it has otherwise proved to be a frustrating few months for the Swede, who has started just one Premier League match for Mikel Arteta’s side so far this season.

Gyokeres amassed a respectable 21 goals in all competitions in his maiden season after arriving from Sporting CP for £64million, but now faces an uncertain future at the Emirates having fallen beneath Kai Havertz in the pecking order.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

With speculation likely to mount ahead of the January window, some pundits, including Micah Richards, have suggested that the Gunners should look to move Gyokeres on.

But former Arsenal striker Aliadiere believes that might be a mistake and ultimately leave Arteta short of options at the top of the pitch.

‘I think it’s all depending on the finances how much they can get for him and who to replace him with,’ Aliadiere told Metro.

‘Because I think as much as obviously he’s not in the top 11 now because Havertz is preferred number one, you don’t want to sell him, get a good price and not be able to replace him.

‘If Havertz gets injured, which obviously we’ve seen in the past – he’s had a few injuries and he can pick up injuries – you just end up with no striker at all.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So I think it’s a very difficult January transfer window. Do you try to buy someone before you sell? I think when you look over the summer, selling Trossard and Martinelli before buying somebody.

‘Obviously, they go to Tzolis, but I’m not sure Tzolis was bought to be the first choice and when he is injured, you end up doing Eze on the left-hand side, and that’s not really his best position in my opinion.

‘So I don’t want it to happen with Gyokeres, thinking let’s try to sell him and recuperate a good transfer fee for him and then not replacing him.’

But even if Gyokeres remains at the club, Aliadiere can’t envisage the 28-year-old becoming the long-term solution to Arsenal’s search for a clinical striker.

‘I just feel the way Arsenal plays does not quite suit Gyokeres’ style of play,’ Aliadiere, speaking via football betting, added.

‘I’ve always been very quite patient and looking at the good stuff that he does, and I still feel that he does some amazing work. But I just do feel that the players don’t really give him the ball quick enough, which is what he needs.

‘He needs to be on 1v1. He needs to run the channel, get fed the ball quite quickly. And I feel we’re not really playing that way. We like to control the ball.

‘We like to control the tempo and just slow down the game. And I just feel Gyokeres is more of a counter-attacking player where he sees the space, he wants it quickly and then he’s on 1v1 and then he can then dominate physically.

‘But he’s rarely getting in that position, so I just find it difficult to kind of see him turning things around in a way of probably just being a rotation player.’

#1881. Galli reveals details of Cardinale’s speech at legends dinner: “Heartfelt and sincere”

Before the Inter game, AC Milan invited several legends to a dinner hosted by Gerry Cardinale to honour them.

In recent years, there has maybe been an avoidance of celebrating the club’s history. Iconic players have been overlooked and the past hasn’t been at the forefront. Of course, the present takes precedence, but it’s almost like the rich history of Milan has been overlooked.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been a few nods to the past, as well as a few kits with historic hints. Yet, you’d be lying if you said that the club were completely honouring the legends that had represented them before.

Now, things are seemingly changing. The Hall of Fame presentation was the most public display of affection, but Cardinale also hosted a dinner for the club’s legends. In attendance of the dinner was Filippo Galli, and he’s offered some information on what happened, praising the American for the event, as MilanNews relays from his interview with Gazzetta dello Sport.

“He spoke for a good half hour, and I found it to be heartfelt and sincere. I’d particularly emphasise the mea culpa for the mistakes made. I’d say it’s a good start; his words seemed heartfelt, and not necessary. But there’s still a long way to go.

“He insisted that he will continue to invest. I’d say he understands how soccer works in Italy, compared to the American one, where everything is more relaxed.

“He then spoke kindly of Berlusconi’s career at the club, emphasising, however, that Berlusconi would now be dealing with a changed world, where financial sustainability becomes vital. Now we’re waiting for something to happen…

“Right now, there’s a January transfer window to address, a technical area to sort out and define. There’s a need to establish high-level governance; otherwise the coach will be left alone, and if by chance the results don’t arrive…

“Did this dinner organised by Cardinale surprise me? Actually, yes, we weren’t expecting it. The invitation came from Milan a couple of weeks earlier. For us, these are opportunities to meet up with former teammates, to represent Milan. And this, regardless of who owns the club.”

#1880. Why Arsenal failed with Max Dowman red card appeal as FA release statement

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman "gave the referee a decision to make" after being sent off against Fleetwood Town last month, a Football Association (FA) commission has found.

The 16-year-old was shown a straight red card late on at Highbury Stadium, compounding a miserable night for the Gunners as they were sent tumbling out of the Carabao Cup at the fourth round by the League Two side on penalties.

Dowman was given his marching orders for kicking out after a heavy challenge from Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal.

As reported by Standard Sport, Arsenal decided to appeal the red card and, as per the BBC, submitted two videos as evidence to the FA's regulatory commission, along with a letter from secretary Zayna Perkins.

However, the appeal was rejected - meaning Dowman must serve a three-match domestic suspension.

Dowman’s sanction was determined by a three-person Independent Regulatory Commission, who have released the written reasons for their decisions.

The majority view accepted that Dowman had received a forceful challenge that he did not see coming, but the two commission members felt he had the option to "step out of this challenge without any reaction but he turned back towards Neal and his forceful attempt at a retaliatory kick gave the referee a decision to make".

The minority view was that Dowman's actions were petulant rather than an act of violent conduct, and "did not constitute a challenge made with excessive force or brutality.”

The forward's age was rejected as a relevant factor in deliberations and the commission could find no "truly exceptional" reason to alter the suspension.

While Arsenal felt a three-game ban was "clearly excessive", the appeal was unanimously rejected by the commission members, who also noted that the threshold for a "clearly excessive" appeal is a high bar to reach.

Dowman served the first of his three-match ban in the win over Liverpool last weekend and will sit out Premier League matches against Hull and Newcastle either side of the November international break.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Vinai Venkatesham has insisted that Tottenham are targeting winning the Champions League under Roberto De Zerbi.

Spurs have finished 17th in the Premier League in each of the past two seasons, narrowly avoiding relegation to the Championship on the final day of last term.

De Zerbi arrived in March to help steer the club to safety after Thomas Frank’s stumbling reign and a disastrous interim period under Igor Tudor.

Tottenham sat winless and bottom of the table at the first international break this season but results have picked up since then. Three successive wins have left them in ninth place ahead of Saturday’s lunchtime trip to Leeds.

Venkatesham is confident that Spurs are now “on the right track” under De Zerbi and the club’s chief executive was ambitious when talking about long-term targets.

Speaking on The Sports Agents podcast, Venkatesham revealed the extremely lofty goals he believes are possible after a period of upheaval to bring in De Zerbi and overhaul the squad.

He said: “Ultimately, I guess the best way to answer your question is what are we here for? We’re here to win, right? The people that we’ve attracted to the football club, the long list of people, everyone is here to win.

“If you work for Tottenham, when we talk about being here to win, that means we’re here to win the Premier League. That’s what this football club wants to do.

#1877. Real Madrid transfer news: First summer 2027 signing already identified with £68m rising star

By Axel Clody | 06 Nov 2026 11:58, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 11:58

The summer 2027 transfer window is a long way off, but Real Madrid already appear to have a file to consider involving a rising star.

Will Nico Paz return to Real Madrid? The Argentine attacking midfielder left the Spanish club in the summer of 2024 to join Como. After two fine seasons in Italy, the 22-year-old was expected back at Real Madrid last summer, as they held a buy-back option. He ultimately refused to return to the Santiago Bernabeu in order to continue his development under Cesc Fabregas.

It was a decision embraced by the Argentina international, and one that has paid off, as he continues to shine at Como. At the start of this season, he has scored six goals and provided eight assists in 13 matches.

Nico Paz is a genuine rising star of world football. To keep him, Como spent £55m (€66m) in total, but Real Madrid still hold the future of the Argentine gem in their hands thanks to a £67m (€80m) buy-back clause.

However, in this case, Fabrizio Romano reports that the clause will only take effect in the summer 2027 transfer window.

If the Spanish giants do not bring back their former starlet next summer, they will lose control over his future for good.

Real Madrid will therefore face an important dilemma. On the one hand, they have every interest in bringing back such a talent to strengthen their attack.

Next summer will be the last time the La Liga side benefit from a preferential price and an advantage over the other suitors. The market value of the Argentine prodigy, already £67m (€80m), is bound to rise year after year as he confirms his full potential at Como.

With regard to a return of Nico Paz to Real Madrid next summer, Romano also reveals that the player himself and Jose Mourinho spoke this summer.

‘Coach, I love Real Madrid and I respect you, but I would rather stay at Como for at least one more season to keep progressing,’ he told the Special One during that video call.

You never know whether Real Madrid’s train will come round again.

The attacking midfielder could therefore seize this potentially final opportunity to return to the Spanish capital, where he has only been able to play eight matches at senior level since the start of his career.

On the other hand, Real Madrid already have Jude Bellingham as their number 10. The Englishman is also young (23) and performing very well. Arda Guler (21), who is also an attacking midfielder by trade, can be added to that. A return for Nico Paz could therefore create a significant logjam in that area.

Jose Mourinho could be forced to move some players to different positions to try to please everyone, with Real Madrid’s attack already well stocked with Vinicius Junior, Mbappe, Rodrygo and Diomande. Unless a major departure occurs, the return of the prodigy could create problems in a dressing room full of egos.

#1871. Tottenham youngster joins Luca Williams-Barnett in first-team training before Leeds clash

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham youngster Jun'ai Byfield has been back training with the first team ahead of Saturday’s trip to Leeds.

The versatile defender - who can play at centre-back, right-back or in midfield - is among the most highly-rated young talents at Spurs having progressed through the academy ranks since the age of eight.

Under-21 regular Byfield was handed his maiden senior Tottenham debut back in January, when former boss Thomas Frank introduced him in place of Lucas Bergvall for the final 28 minutes of a 2-0 home Champions League win over Borussia Dortmund.

He was also sent on as a substitute a week later for the closing stages of a victory at Eintracht Frankfurt that saw Spurs seal a place in the last 16.

Byfield has made one Premier League appearance so far for Tottenham, introduced again late off the bench by Frank during the dramatic 2-2 draw with Manchester City.

However, his progress has been hampered of late by injury, with the 17-year-old having been sidelined since May and missed pre-season completely before returning as a substitute for the U21s during their EFL Trophy clash with fourth-tier Cheltenham that was most notable for the shock selection of exiled striker Richarlison.

Byfield has been building his fitness since then and was seen in a club video posted to social media returning to first-team training at Tottenham on Thursday, alongside fellow youngster Luca Williams-Barnett, who was handed his own Premier League debut by head coach Roberto De Zerbi during last weekend’s win over Crystal Palace.

It remains to be seen if De Zerbi will consider Byfield for a potential first-team role in the months ahead, with the likes of Tyrese Hall having also impressed the Spurs boss during a recent warm-weather training camp in Marbella, alongside Tye Hall and Callum Olusesi.

Tottenham are expected to receive plenty of interest in their talented crop of youngsters during the January transfer window, including goalkeeper Luca Gunter and U21s captain James Rowswell.

Former England Lioness Mary Earps has revealed the birth of a ‘secret’ baby boy with her partner Kitty Forrest.

#1868. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is one of football's great talents... so why can't he get games in this struggling Celtic side?

Published: 16:18 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 2 November 2026

How has it come to this for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, one of the most gifted and decorated England internationals of his generation?

Here, after all, is a midfielder whose precocious talent as a teenager at Southampton went on to earn him a full house of English trophies.

In six years with Arsenal and six with Liverpool, there was also a Champions League winner’s medal and 35 caps for his country.

And yet now, at the age of 33, he finds himself struggling to get games for a Celtic side who are a shadow of their former selves, especially in Europe.

Used only sparingly this season, the Ox was given a rare start against Falkirk yesterday, when he was preferred to Benjamin Nygren.

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill said he needed someone with experience to take care of the ball but the Englishman was substituted 65 minutes into a 2-0 defeat.

Celtic midfielder Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was given a rare start in the defeat by Falkirk

The Englishman has made only eight appearances in Martin O'Neill's team this season

It will not have escaped Oxlade-Chamberlain’s notice that former club Besiktas are Celtic’s next opponents in the Europa League on Thursday night.

The midfielder’s recent travails can be traced back to his move to Turkey in 2023, after Liverpool deemed him surplus to requirements.

His first few months at Besiktas went well enough, but he was soon sidelined by injury, as he had frequently been at Anfield, and his career in Turkey was already on the slide.

Concerned by his fitness and his salary, Besiktas wanted to offload him but he stayed another season and found himself frozen out by manager Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

Although Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was more willing to give him opportunities, his contract was terminated in July and it wasn’t until the following February that he found another club.

That club was Celtic, so plagued by crises on and off the pitch that they were happy to secure him on a short-term deal, even if he was a little rusty.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made all the right noises, describing Celtic as the ‘perfect fit’, the kind of club whose size and expectation he was used to.

And sure enough, he scored a late winner on his debut against Livingston and helped his new team to a double, albeit the most troubled one in their long history. He then signed a one-year contract extension and spoke of looking forward to his first proper pre-season in three years.

Oxlade-Chamberlain won the Premier League and Champions League in his time at Liverpool

It hasn’t done him much good. So far, he has made only eight appearances, four of them from the start. O’Neill seems loath to rotate a midfield in which Callum McGregor is over-used.

You can’t have the world at your feet forever, but a little more game time was expected for a player who is two years younger than James Forrest.

Maybe all those injuries have caught up with him. Maybe his playing style isn’t best suited to the ageing process. In his prime, he was explosive, strong and adept at breaking the lines, whereas now the priority is to stay fit.

Or perhaps he is just another victim of the Celtic curse that befalls Premier League stars who venture north in the twilight of their careers.

From Middlesbrough’s Brazilian World Cup winner Juninho, to Arsenal greats Ian Wright and Freddie Ljungberg, there are more than a few who have come a cropper in Glasgow’s east end.

Oxlade-Chamberlain isn’t in that category, but he has work to do if his veteran stardust is to have any chance of disguising the deep-rooted problems at Celtic Park. He needs a chance, and he needs to take it… sooner rather than later.

#1867. Thomas Tuchel explains why Arsenal star handed shock England snub

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thomas Tuchel has explained his “difficult decision” to leave Arsenal winger Noni Madueke out of the latest England squad.

Despite having been one of Tuchel’s trusted men at the World Cup in the summer, Madueke was on Friday omitted for Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

The snub comes after England team-mate Bukayo Saka’s quad injury had given Madueke a greater opportunity to impress for Arsenal on the right flank of late.

He has played more in recent weeks and scored important goals against Nottingham Forest in the Premier League and Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

But despite call-ups for Arsenal team-mates Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ben White and Eberechi Eze, Madueke was left out by England this time.

“It was a close call and a difficult decision not to bring Noni, because he got his minutes after Bukayo’s injury at Arsenal,” Tuchel said at a post-squad selection press conference at Wembley.

“He got some goals. It was very close. But also [in that position], we stuck with the group that we had [during the last international break] and give them our trust.”

White was injured during the last international window so not available for selection.

He was England’s only goalscorer in March, when he made his first appearances for the national team since leaving the 2022 World Cup squad in Qatar during Gareth Southgate’s tenure for personal reasons.

White was booed by some sections of the England fanbase during friendlies against Uruguay and Japan at Wembley, but Tuchel saw that as no reason to omit him from this month’s squad now the player is back fit.

“We were not happy about this,” Tuchel said on the boos for White, who also missed out on a World Cup place due to injury. “We could understand the disappointment of the fans, of course, with what had happened before. But I think this is expressed [by] now and should be a closed book.

“I think everyone could also see the investment of Ben and the quality of Ben and how he presented himself in the March camp. He did excellently, scored for us, and then committed a foul where we conceded a penalty.”

Tuchel continued: “When I speak to him, I always feel the hunger from him to come back. He missed the last camp. He is the standout position for Arsenal in a position where we struggle with injuries somehow.

#1865. Cray Wanderers vs Stockport County - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 06 Nov 2026 12:50, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 12:56

The oldest football club in London will hope to create history in the world's oldest cup competition on Sunday afternoon when seventh-tier Cray Wanderers welcome League One side Stockport County to a sold-out Flamingo Park.

The Wands have progressed through several qualifying rounds to reach the FA Cup First Round Proper, earning a tie against a Hatters side who climbed to second in the league after beating Wimbledon 2-1 last weekend.

Having played seven matches in the FA Cup this season, four of which ended level after 90 minutes, with three requiring replays, Cray Wanderers have reached the First Round Proper for the first time in their 166-year history, having been founded before the competition itself.

Entering the competition in the First Qualifying Round, the Wands overcame Lewes, Maidstone United, Chippenham Town and, most recently, Bedford Town to set up Sunday's historic encounter.

Led by Tim O'Shea, who made three league appearances for Tottenham Hotspur during the 1980s, Cray's most recent tie saw them draw with Bedford after 90 minutes before finding another equaliser in extra time to take the contest to a penalty shootout.

The Wands subsequently prevailed 4-3 on penalties to create a moment of history and have since returned to league action, where they compete at Step 3 of the National League System and currently sit just one place above the relegation zone in the Isthmian League Premier Division.

However, their league position does not fully reflect the four wins, three draws and three defeats they have recorded from their opening 10 matches, with their impressive FA Cup run forcing several fixtures to be postponed and rearranged.

As a result, O'Shea's side have as many as seven games in hand on some of their fellow seventh-tier sides.

As for Stockport County, they make the journey to Chislehurst looking to avoid what could prove to be one of the biggest FA Cup upsets of the season.

Led by Jimmy McNulty, the Hatters have enjoyed an impressive run of form in League One, with four victories from their last six matches lifting them to second in the table, just three points behind the league leaders.

Stockport's FA Cup campaign came to an end in the second round last season following a 5-4 penalty shootout defeat to Cambridge United, although they faced Premier League opposition in Crystal Palace during the 2024-25 campaign, eventually suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat to the eventual cup winners.

More recently, the Greater Manchester outfit have been adjusting to life under new manager McNulty after long-serving boss Dave Challinor departed in the summer following their playoff final defeat to Bolton Wanderers.

The Hatters are hoping to return to the second tier for the first time since 2002 and, with a long season still ahead, will be determined to keep their promotion ambitions on track while avoiding an unwanted cup exit this weekend.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Ade Yussuff scored two of Cray's four goals in their most recent outing, and the striker, who has found the net 12 times this season, is expected to lead the line for the hosts on Sunday afternoon.

The Wands are also likely to retain JJ Briggs in goal, while captain Frankie Raymond is expected to continue at full-back.

As for visiting Stockport County, McNulty could make wholesale changes as his side prepare to face opponents who sit 111 league places below them in the football pyramid.

The Hatters boss may choose to rest key players such as Jack Diamond and Kyle Wootton, potentially opening the door for teenage forward Che Gardner and French striker Mikael Mandron to feature from the start.

Regular goalkeeper Oliver Whatmuff could also make way for Luca Ashby-Hammond, who has featured twice in the EFL Trophy this season.

Brad Hills and Kyron Gordon will, however, play no part in this weekend's cup tie due to injury.

Briggs; Lema, Strachan, Morgan, Raymond; McLeod, Adaja, Ogunwamide, Hernandez; Yusuff, Ufuah

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Ashby-Hammond; Jobe, O'Connell, Pye; Dacres-Cogley, Norwood, Fiorini, Ennis; Gardner, Mandron, Edun

While Sunday promises to be a historic occasion for one of the country's oldest football clubs, we expect Stockport County to have far too much quality for their non-league opponents.

The League One outfit boast one of the most prolific attacks in the English Football League, and we expect McNulty's men to demonstrate the gulf in quality by securing a comfortable victory and booking their place in the next round.

#1864. Thomas Tuchel doubles down on Cole Palmer warning as England snub explained

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Thomas Tuchel has explained why Cole Palmer was left out of the latest England squad, repeating his belief that the Chelsea star “misses too many opportunities to impress” for his country.

Palmer was on Friday the headline omission from Tuchel’s 25-man squad to contest this month’s Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

That was despite England staff checking with Chelsea on his fitness this week in the lead-up to the squad being finalised. It is understood that Palmer is fit and was available for selection.

Having missed the World Cup in the summer, Palmer was initially picked for the last England squad in September, but withdrew due to an injury which Chelsea said they needed to manage.

While Tuchel acknowledged at the time that the issue was genuine, he did not hide his disappointment and remarked that Palmer “misses too many opportunities” to play for England.

Of Tuchel’s 26 matches in charge so far, Palmer has featured in only three. The England head coach was asked at a press conference at Wembley on Friday why Palmer had been overlooked.

“It’s enough No10s and we stick to the guys who were in camp [last time],” Tuchel explained. “The impact of all the players was immense.

“We have Josh King as a new player. He can play all four [attacking] positions. That’s basically the reason. He gives us a bit of flexibility.

“In the pre-season, he [King] helped us in training as a full-back. We will not try that again.”

Tuchel provided further detail about Palmer’s situation, insisting: “Everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception.

“But, again, what I said last time: he misses too many opportunities to impress. Two-and-a-half weeks was a long time [to miss]. The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided [to go] without him.”

There was a first senior England call-up for Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude.

Tuchel hinted that Jobe Bellingham could come into his thinking as he plots out his midfield selection for the clash with Croatia next week.

“Myles [Lewis-Skelly] is suspended for the first game against Croatia, so there is an opportunity [for Jobe] - coming on his own pathway,” he said.

Tuchel then explained why Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, much-tipped for a maiden England call by team-mates at Everton and manager David Moyes, had not been selected.

“[He was ] close, a very good player,” Tuchel said. “I see him as an offensive No8 or more as a No10.

“As you know, he is in our squad of 55. He is a standout player for Everton; you see his quality. He was very close.”

Nevertheless, Ruben Amorim saw things differently, believing he could play a role. Of course, he’s not the only player who he offered an opportunity to, but he may be the best example of things changing.

The Nigerian was pivotal to Amorim’s system, being the starting wing-back on the right for most of the early season. Unfortunately, though, he suffered a hip injury and hasn’t been seen since.

As confirmed in recent minutes by a club statement, Chukwueze’s surgery has now taken place and it was a complete success. A return date has not been given, but reports from the time of the injury suggested he’d be back in 2027.

“AC Milan announces that Samuel Chukwueze has undergone surgery in London to repair a ruptured tendon in the tensor fascia latae muscle in his left hip. The surgery, performed by Prof. Ernest Schilders in the presence of Dr. Stefano Mazzoni, was a complete success.
